ce912a408f131545: NEW YORK: President Donald Trump's administration asked the US Supreme Court on Wednesday to let it proceed with a plan to build a US-Mexico border barrier in a remote region of West Texas that includes Big Bend National Park.

The Justice Department filed an emergency request asking the court to lift a federal judge's order halting wall construction in the region while a lawsuit against the project, brought by an environmental group and other challengers, proceeds.
The Republican president has long touted building or reinforcing barriers along the US-Mexico border as a signature part of his anti-immigration policies.

But his administration's push to extend border infrastructure into the national park, about 400km southeast of El Paso, has faced opposition from local officials, conservationists and some Texas Republicans.

The lawsuit was brought by the Center for Biological Diversity, a Big Bend-area river guide and a group seeking to preserve a historic church in Ruidosa, Texas, which says its fragile adobe structure is threatened by the border construction.

The plaintiffs challenged a series of waivers issued by the US Department of Homeland Security to expedite the construction of roads and barriers in the Big Bend region, bypassing various environmental and conservation laws.

Former Homeland Security secretary Kristi Noem and current secretary Markwayne Mullin, who issued the waivers between February and July, found the region to be an "area of high illegal entry", requiring additional barriers to control the border.

US District Judge Kathleen Cardone in El Paso issued an injunction on Oct 2 halting construction. In an opinion issued later, the judge found that the waivers exceeded the authority of Noem and Mullin.
The Justice Department urged the Supreme Court to pause or overturn Cardone's injunction.

"Even assuming that the secretary's waiver authority implicates a question of 'vast economic and political significance,' Congress did clearly authorise the secretary both to build border barriers and to waive legal requirements in order to facilitate their expeditious construction," the Justice Department wrote.
In August, the administration paused construction in Big Bend after the project drew bipartisan criticism over its potential impact on the park's landscape and wildlife.
Crews had begun clearing land in the park for roads and border security infrastructure, prompting protests and lawsuits seeking to halt the work.
ad6b97d5a179e794: PARIS: Manchester United were hammered 4-1 by Como in the Champions League on Wednesday as the pressure increased on beleaguered manager Michael Carrick, while a late Declan Rice equaliser earned Arsenal a 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich.
Elsewhere, Real Madrid thumped RB Leipzig 4-1 and there were also notable victories for Inter Milan, Aston Villa and Real Betis.
The most remarkable scoreline, though, came in driving rain on the banks of Lake Como, where United suffered their joint-heaviest loss in the Champions League in the last 30 years.

Nico Paz scored twice for Cesc Fabregas's Como, with Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramon getting their other goals. This was a second 4-1 home win in this season's competition for the tournament debutants.
Joshua Zirkzee pulled one back at the death for United, but they are now seven games without a win in all competitions.
The Red Devils have just one win in the Premier League this season and have now suffered back-to-back losses in Europe. Carrick's position risks becoming untenable.
"I have not given my own position any thought," Carrick said.
"For us to play in that way, it's not acceptable. It wasn't a good performance at all," he admitted.
Last season's beaten finalists Arsenal have seven points from a possible nine after Rice struck in the 82nd minute to earn a draw in Munich.
Bukayo Saka went off injured early on but his replacement Eberechi Eze fired Arsenal into the lead, only for Alphonso Davies to level before the interval.
Harry Kane set up that goal with a magnificent pass and then gave Bayern the lead from a second-half penalty, his 10th strike this season in all competitions.
But Arsenal hit back as Bayern registered a second straight Champions League stalemate.
"We looked dangerous, we got the goal and we had a moment there where we could have killed off the game," Kane told broadcaster DAZN.
"Probably a draw was a fair result overall... There's a lot of games and we've got players with injuries, players missing tonight, so we take the point and move on."
Real three from three

Jose Mourinho's Real are one of five teams with three wins from three in this season's Champions League, as goals either side of half-time from Bernardo Silva and Arda Guler set them on their way at the Bernabeu.
Kylian Mbappe made it 12 goals in 12 games this season for Real before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back, but Yan Diomande completed Real's victory with a spectacular volley against his former club.
"We know every point is important to get into the top eight, we know we have to win as many games as possible – we've won three and there are five to go," Mbappe told Movistar.
Villa also have a perfect record after three games, as they won 3-1 at home to Viking Stavanger with Ross Barkley's opener being followed by Emiliano Buendia's penalty and Henrik Heggheim's own goal.
Peter Christiansen got one back for the Norwegian champions who are still looking for their first win.
Inter had Alessandro Bastoni sent off midway through the second half before Carlos Augusto's late goal secured a 1-0 win at home to Shakhtar Donetsk, as the Italian champions got their first points.
Betis have maximum points as an Isco penalty handed them a 1-0 win over Feyenoord in Seville.
PSG blow
Club Brugge defeated Lens 3-0 in Belgium as Hans Vanaken, Joaquin Seys and Carlos Forbs all found the net.
Victor Osimhen sealed a 4-2 victory for Galatasaray away to his old side Lille in France, after earlier efforts from Yunus Akgun and Aleksey Batrakov and a Nabil Bentaleb own goal.
Teenager Soriba Diaoune got both goals for Lille, who have lost three out of three.
LASK of Austria have their first points after a fine 3-2 victory over Sporting in Lisbon.
Luis Suarez scored twice for Sporting, including an early penalty, but Christoph Lang, Sasa Kalajdzic and Krystof Danek all netted in between for the visitors.

Reigning champions PSG are top of the 36-team standings after beating Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday, but the French side confirmed Wednesday that star winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in that game.
He will undergo surgery in the coming days amid doubts as to whether he will play again this season.

7fe366b1bba98d85: BIRMINGHAM: Aston Villa maintained their perfect start to the Champions League on Wednesday, cruising to a 3-1 win against Norwegian side Viking to strengthen their push for a top-eight finish in the league phase.
Ross Barkley put the dominant home side ahead midway through the first half and Emiliano Buendia stroked home a penalty to double their lead at Villa Park.
An own goal from Henrik Heggheim shortly after the hour mark made the game all but safe for Villa, though the visitors grabbed a late consolation.
"We played a very safe match," Villa boss Unai Emery told TNT Sports. "First half we dominated, we were feeling comfortable.
"The second half we started not like the first half and conceded some corners. In 90 minutes overall we were better and dominated more than less.
"We're so happy how we're getting those three points."
Emery's new-look team have now won all of their opening three Champions League matches following a 3-2 victory against Club Brugge and a 6-0 mauling of Fenerbahce.
An upturn in fortunes in the Premier League means Villa have now won five out of six games in all competitions – a dramatic turnaround after a slow start to the season.
Viking drew 3-3 with six-time European champions Bayern Munich last week but the home team were dominant from the start on Wednesday.
Nicolas Jackson had two free headers, both of which he directed tamely at goalkeeper Arild Ostbo.
The opener came in the 23rd minute when midfielder Barkley rose to nod home Ibrahim Mbaye's corner.
Villa doubled their lead from the penalty spot in the 37th minute when Zlatko Tripic was penalised for a foul on Alysson after a VAR review. Buendia stepped up and nonchalantly stroked the ball home.
The visitors started the second half brightly, forcing Villa back, but Alysson was inches away from extending Villa's lead.
And they had a three-goal cushion after Heggheim deflected Alysson's effort into the net following a swift counter-attack.
Peter Christiansen gave the away fans something to cheer in the final few minutes with a superb volley following a cross from the right.
Victory leaves Villa well placed to finish in the top eight, which would guarantee direct qualification for the last 16 of Europe's top club competition.
Villa enjoyed an outstanding 2025/26 season, finishing fourth in the Premier League and winning the Europa League – their first major trophy for 30 years.

Emery was faced with the task of a huge rebuild after a series of high-profile departures during the summer transfer window, including Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa, Emiliano Martinez, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne.
But his new side is rapidly taking shape, helped by new signings such as Jackson and Switzerland forward Johan Manzambi, who missed Wednesday's match with an injury.

de0a8bfaf7a94744: MUNICH: Arsenal coach Mikel Arteta said the club was "concerned" about the severity of an injury to winger Bakayo Saka after Wednesday's pulsating 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern Munich.
Saka, Arsenal's joint top goalscorer this season alongside Victor Gyokeres, went off early after falling to the turf grabbing his thigh and was replaced by Eberechi Eze.
Eze scored Arsenal's opener and Declan Rice scored late to clinch a draw for last season's runners up after an Alphonso Davies goal and a Harry Kane penalty for the hosts.
Arteta said Saka's injury was as yet unclear, but told reporters the club's medical staff were worried.
"They are a bit concerned about Saka. When a player has to come off with sharp pain it is never good news. We have to wait and see," Arteta said.
The coach spoke glowingly of his side's efforts, while praising those of the home side.
"Bayern batter every team, so I really value what the boys did tonight," he said.
"That's one of the highest levels we have played... The level of opposition and our level as well. It was two teams that wanted to attack and play."
Rice was thrilled with his late goal.
"I'm so happy. When you play against teams like Bayern that are man-to-man all over the pitch, you have to apply certain principles," Rice told TNT.
"I just kept running, lost my marker and I was in on goal to score."
d3c1cf3f72014cef: SAN FRANCISCO: Meta beat investor expectations for third-quarter revenue on Wednesday but the social media giant's profits took a hit due to an US$18 billion legal settlement with nearly all US states.
The company reported US$9.86 billion in profits from July to September, almost 50% below investor expectations, which Meta said was dragged down by a US$9.9 billion charge related to the settlement.
Meta reported its earnings just hours after another financial penalty was announced related to a case in New Mexico.
A judge ruled that Meta must pay US$25 billion to New Mexico after a jury found last month that the social media giant had deceived users in a case related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal.
The company has also been spending aggressively to build out its artificial intelligence capabilities.
In the September quarter, Meta said it spent US$35 billion on capital expenditures, below investor expectations of US$41 billion.
In July the company had increased its spending estimate for the whole year to US$145 billion, up from US$130 billion, which is nearly double what it spent in 2025.

41e5ac5f94246c77: MUNICH: Declan Rice scored a late equaliser to grab last season's runners-up Arsenal a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday.
Eberechi Eze opened the scoring for Arsenal after coming on for the injured Bukayo Saka but Alphonso Davies brought Bayern level after a sublime pass from Harry Kane.
Kane put Bayern on track for victory when he converted a second-half penalty, but his England teammate Rice equalised with eight minutes remaining to earn Arsenal a point.
The Gunners have seven points from three games in the league phase, two more than Bayern.
Bayern were without in-form winger Michael Olise, Germany captain Joshua Kimmich and midfielder Jamal Musiala. Coach Vincent Kompany had been a doubt due to illness but took his place in the dugout.
"We looked dangerous, we got the goal and we had a moment there where we could have killed off the game," Kane told DAZN.
"Probably a draw was a fair result overall... There's a lot of games and we've got players with injuries, players missing tonight, so we take the point and move on."

Despite the absences, the England captain ensured Bayern posed a consistent threat against Arsenal's miserly defence with another excellent performance ahead of next week's Ballon d'Or ceremony in Kane's hometown of London.

Kane's second-half penalty, his 16th goal in 23 matches against Arsenal, extended his scoring streak to 10 straight Champions League games. Kane is one shy of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo, who scored in 11 consecutive matches for Real Madrid.

"I had an amazing season last year, I'm extremely proud of it. The Ballon d'Or would be amazing to win, but there's nothing I can do, the voting closed a long time ago, I have to wait for the night and see what happens," Kane said of the award.
The draw was just the second time Arsenal had dropped points in 12 games in all competitions this season.

"The manager has drilled into us for the last two days we're not just coming in to sit and hit on the counter - we wanted to match them all over the pitch," Rice told TNT Sports. "At home, they're one of the best teams in Europe with Paris."
Arsenal forward Kai Havertz felt the result was fair.
"I think it was a top-notch game for both sides," he said. "We can be proud of our performance, especially since it's anything but easy to hold your own here."
Early Saka blow
Arsenal were hit with an early blow when Saka fell to the ground eight minutes in, grabbing his thigh and immediately signalling to the bench.

Bayern's two previous Champions League opponents were from Norway and the perennial Bundesliga winners seemed to struggle with Arsenal's physicality as Mikel Arteta's side pinned them back in the early stages.
With 25 minutes gone, Odegaard floated a simple pass across Bayern's defence and into the path of the onrushing Eze, who collected and stroked the ball past Manuel Neuer.
Caught out by Eze's perfectly timed run, the hosts looked even more surprised when VAR overturned the linesman's offside call and awarded the goal.
The pre-match chatter had been dominated by talk of Kane's Ballon d'Or prospects and he showed why he is among the favourites when he set up Davies's equaliser 10 minutes later.
Kane spotted Davies on the move and threaded the ball through the midfield and around Gabriel for the Canadian winger to guide the ball into the bottom corner.
With the hosts now in the ascendancy, Ezri Konsa saw yellow for taking Kane out of a Bayern counter minutes later.
After the break, Neuer and David Raya took turns producing magnificent saves, with the Bayern captain tipping Bruno Guimaraes's header onto the crossbar and the Spaniard denying Dayot Upamecano.
Both sides traded surges forward but Kane would again prove crucial as Bayern took the lead.
Kane's shot from the edge of the penalty area connected with Jurrien Timber's arm, the referee immediately pointing to the spot before Kane stepped up and buried his kick.
Bayern looked to be in control but the match turned again when late substitute Viktor Gyokeres threaded a clever pass to Rice, who slammed in an equaliser.

The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) offers a competitive alternative to express buses and flights for time-conscious travellers, but families may find the combined ticket costs less attractive, transport experts said.

Universiti Malaya Centre for Transportation Research head Associate Professor Dr Yuen Choon Wah said the fares were attractive for students and solo travellers, with the journey from Gombak to Kota Baru expected to take about five hours compared with more than eight by bus.
"Even with train fares of RM125 compared with bus fares of RM50-plus, I still think it is worth the money," he said, adding that the service could encourage more travellers to switch to rail.
But he had doubts about whether the ECRL could attract group travellers, as the combined cost of tickets could make other options more economical.
One-way fares from Gombak to KotaSAS start at RM60 for the Transit service and RM68 for the Express service, while fares to Kota Baru start at RM125 (Transit) and RM147 (Express).
In comparison, express bus fares from Kuala Lumpur to Kota Baru range from RM34 to RM65, while premium services and peak-period tickets can cost up to RM105.
One-way flights between Kuala Lumpur and Kota Baru can range from RM89 to RM350 or more.

Universiti Teknologi Mara Faculty of Film, Theatre and Animation's Associate Professor Dr Mohd Syuhaidi Abu Bakar said the fares were reasonable and competitive when journey time, comfort and convenience were considered.
"Some people may consider the fares expensive, but we have to consider the time saved, the comfort and convenience."
He said road journeys to Kelantan could take long hours, particularly along the Kuala Lipis-Merapoh-Gua Musang trunk road.
During festive seasons, such journeys can take over 16 hours.
He said the ECRL could provide a good alternative, although affordability would remain an important consideration.
Malaysia Institute of Transport director Associate Professor Dr Mohd Fathi Abu Yaziz @ Mohamad said the ECRL should not be assessed solely on fares, but also on reliability, comfort and time savings.
"The service can bridge the gap between air travel and road transport by providing a faster alternative to buses without the airport procedures."
He cautioned that dynamic pricing could affect affordability for lower-income passengers.
He suggested a hybrid pricing model, with measures such as regulated fare caps or concessions, to balance revenue considerations with the need to keep rail travel accessible.

SEMPORNA: A tiny crustacean found in a submerged cave off Pulau Sipadan has turned out to be from a new species and an entirely new genus.
Named Sipadanomolgus dissimilis, the copepod was collected using a light trap inside the marine cave called Turtle Tomb at the world-renowned diving destination.

Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia's Associate Professor Dr Azman Abdul Rahim, who led the research, said: "The researchers established an entirely new genus, Sipadanomolgus, as the specimen exhibits a distinct combination of anatomical features that does not fit the existing genera within the family."

The research was conducted under the Ocean Census programme, a global initiative to document marine life, in collaboration with Dr Chaichat Boonyanusith of Nakhon Ratchasima Rajabhat University and Dr Koraon Wongkamhaeng of Kasetsart University, both in Thailand.
The findings were published in the European Journal of Taxonomy on Tuesday.
The discovery builds on previous finds in Turtle Tomb, underscoring the scientific value of exploring specialised marine habitats.
Azman said it also broadened understanding of Sipadan's biodiversity beyond its famous coral reefs and larger marine animals, highlighting the role of less visible, cave-dwelling organisms.

KUALA LUMPUR: Women account for more than 34.4 per cent of board seats among Malaysia's top 100 publicly listed companies, but the next challenge is ensuring their representation translates into greater influence over corporate strategy and decision-making.

The 30% Club Malaysia said corporate leaders must move beyond meeting diversity targets to building boardrooms where women's perspectives help shape business priorities, strengthen governance and drive sustainable growth.

Its chair and PwC Malaysia executive chair, Nurul A'in Abdul Latif, said aspiring women directors needed greater access to professional networks, sponsorship and boardroom exposure to prepare them for leadership roles.

"Through mentorship and meaningful connections, the Board Mentoring Scheme (BMS) helps develop a sustainable pipeline of board-ready women who can contribute effectively in governance and leadership roles."
She said achieving gender-balanced leadership required male allies to sponsor talent and create more inclusive pathways to leadership.
She was speaking at the organisation's annual Board Mentoring Celebration on Tuesday, themed "Beyond the Numbers: From Representation to Real Influence".
The event marked the completion of the programme's 11th cohort, comprising 15 women, and welcomed 24 participants to its 12th cohort.
Established with PwC Malaysia in 2017, the nine-month BMS pairs aspiring women leaders with experienced board directors to boost their governance knowledge and professional networks.

The scheme has supported more than 179 senior women leaders across 11 cohorts, with 47 per cent securing board positions in public-listed companies, small and medium enterprises, and industry associations.

30% Club Malaysia steering committee member and PwC Malaysia partner Pauline Ho said board diversity should be measured by whether women's views influenced organisational decisions, rather than representation alone.

WASHINGTON: United Nations experts called on Tuesday for an independent investigation into Indian authorities' conduct in a recent crackdown on protests, where they said demonstrators sustained injuries and some reported being subjected to ill-treatment.

Opposition parties and student organisations held protests in recent weeks, demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter ​lists that they say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Mass protests also took place in the summer over exam-paper leaks and led to the resignation of the education minister.

"Despite the non-violent nature of the assemblies, law enforcement agencies have reportedly deployed force against unarmed students, including lathi charges, and have prevented thousands from joining the protests," the two dozen independent experts said, referring to batons used to break up crowds.

"We call on the authorities to immediately cease the use of excessive force, rescind blanket assembly bans and refrain from the misuse of digital surveillance, including through biometrics, and Internet disruptions."

India has dismissed such criticism and cast it as interference in its internal affairs, including when the UN human rights office this month expressed concerns over mass detentions over the latest protests.
The government said this month that law enforcement acted "strictly in accordance with the law".

Protesting groups said the removal of 130 million names from voter lists led to eligible voters being disenfranchised, which disproportionately affected poor and homeless people, as well as ethnic minorities, including Muslims, who are unlikely to vote for the Hindu nationalist BJP.
The BJP ​and the Election Commission deny this.
The commission said it was removing duplicate, deceased, shifted and otherwise ineligible voters and that anyone excluded in error could pursue appeals.

LONDON: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has accused Cristiano Ronaldo of letting the team down during his tenure at the club.
Portugal star Ronaldo was in his second spell at United when Ten Hag was hired in 2022.
Ten Hag's relationship with Ronaldo quickly became tense, and the striker refused to come on as a substitute in a win over Tottenham in October 2022.
Ronaldo was dropped for a subsequent match against Chelsea, prompting him to give an explosive television interview in which he said he felt betrayed by United and did not respect Ten Hag.
United mutually terminated the former Real Madrid forward's contract the following month.
"He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him," Ten Hag said in an interview with The Athletic.
"Obviously, he's one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire in."
Ten Hag said Ronaldo pulled out of training sessions and did not complete the full run that players were set after they were beaten 4-0 by Brentford early in his reign.

"I confronted him with this. Many times I say, 'Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can't bring yourself in the box, you can't score'. He was not capable of doing this," Ten Hag said.
"It's the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he's exhausted. But he couldn't.
"He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was that he didn't prepare himself."
Ten Hag also said promises made by United's hierarchy went unfulfilled before he was sacked in 2024, shortly after signing a new contract.
Although United won the FA Cup just months earlier with a surprise final victory against Manchester City, Ten Hag was axed with the team languishing in 14th place in the Premier League.
The Dutchman blamed the United hierarchy for some of his problems, saying he was left humiliated when Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay was sold to Napoli without his consent.
Ten Hag also said he wanted to sign Harry Kane, Declan Rice and Frenkie de Jong during his spell at United.
"They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned. We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn't keep," he said.
"I said, 'No selling Scott McTominay'. But they sold him. I got, of course, very embarrassed and disappointed."

Popular Indonesian actor and director Baim Wong has publicly backed Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman following the politician's passionate speech about severe air pollution at the Dewan Rakyat recently.
Sharing a video clip of Syed Saddiq's speech on Threads, the 'Benci Bilang Cinta' star called on the Indonesian government to take swift action over the transboundary haze.
"I must speak up because I care deeply about this country," Wong wrote, showing his support for Syed Saddiq.

The actor accused reckless individuals of starting forest fires in his country, and the haze has damaged Indonesia's reputation abroad besides inflicting serious health and financial hardship on people in the region.
"Our national reputation suffers, trust from other countries declines, economic regression sets in, and ultimately, it's the ordinary people who pay the price.
"Even someone like me, who knows little about politics, can understand this, so why aren't those in power taking action?"
Syed Saddiq had called for Asean members, especially Malaysia and Singapore, to lodge diplomatic protests and take legal action against those responsible for open burning.

bafdf0b555117b83: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff faced criticism Wednesday for calling Vladimir Putin a "humanitarian" despite the Russian leader's brutal war in Ukraine.
Witkoff made the comments as he met Putin in Saint Petersburg to secure the release of Stephen Hubbard, an American citizen who was detained for years after being arrested in Ukraine.
"You talk so much about my president, president Trump, being a humanitarian -- you are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that," Witkoff said, referring to Hubbard's release.
"I commend you, and I thank you again."
The Kremlin said after the meeting between Witkoff and Putin that Russia was ready in principle to rejoin three-way talks with Ukraine and the United States to end the war.
But Witkoff's comments come as Trump's recent pivot away from Ukraine and towards Putin -- the man who launched the biggest war in Europe since World War II -- faces growing scrutiny.
Republican Senator Thom Tillis, a frequent Trump critic in recent months, reacted with astonishment.
"WTF, Steve? Look up the definition of 'humanitarian'," he said in a post on X.
Trump brushed off the comments by Witkoff -- a business friend whom he appointed roving envoy for the Ukraine, Iran and Gaza conflicts after he took office last year.

"Well, I guess you could say (it) for that particular purpose, for the purpose of allowing a man who was thinking he was going to be in prison for life out," Trump said when asked about his envoy's remarks.
"But you know, I wouldn't say anything one way or the other."
US vice-president JD Vance defended Witkoff's comments.
"I agree with Steve Witkoff saying something nice to a person who just released an American hostage," Vance said at an event in Ohio.
"Whether you agree with the underlying sentiment or not, Steve Witkoff is a diplomat. His job is to go over there and get a job done."

ddbc280478901f4d: Peter Steinberger, member of technical staff at OpenAI and the creator of OpenClaw, estimates that he spent around $10 million in tokens running AI workloads last month. But don't feel bad for him, because it's all coming out of investors' pockets.
He made this admission at the Cloudflare Connect 2026 conference in San Francisco on Wednesday, in a conversation with Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht.
Knecht previously observed that Steinberger has acknowledged having "a virtually unlimited token budget, which not all of us in the room have."
Responding to the audible surprise rising from the audience, Steinberger added, "What people don't always understand is not all of that is useful."
That only amplified the murmuring, perhaps not the effect he had been after. Meanwhile, his employer, OpenAI, is reportedly trying to "accelerate funding" ahead of rival Anthropic's expected IPO.
Steinberger's subsequent musing about his preferred way of working failed to recognize Knecht's acknowledgement of financial limitations.

"I feel like the main challenge a lot of people still have is that our infrastructure structure hasn't really caught up yet," Steinberger said. "Like why is this still using my computer? Shouldn't this all be in the cloud?"

Apart from the privacy and compliance implications of relying on cloud-based AI, cost remains a consideration for anyone not setting venture funds alight. Cloud-hosted agents can be expensive. Shouldn't this all run locally?

Pointing to the OpenClaw project and how a lot of open source maintainers have given up accepting pull requests due to frustration with AI slop, Knecht asked Steinberger whether we're approaching the death of open source or a golden age of AI.
Steinberger said he thinks the way pull requests are handled needs to change because people don't explain how they arrived at their proposed changed code.
"If I see your thoughts, how you got from A to B, my trust in the output is way higher than if you just throw the finished work across the fence," he said.
Knecht also asked Steinberger whether everyone in the room would have hundreds of AI agents running in a few years.
Steinberger doubts it will be hundreds.

"I think everyone will have some sort of intelligence that runs and thinks and helps them throughout the day or even predicts what could help you in the future," he said. "So instead of asking the question, maybe you already get the answer."
Toward the end of the session, Knecht raised the issue of trust and how to know what data to give to an agent.

That's a hard question, Steinberger admitted. Part of it, he said, has to do with how much you trust the underlying model itself, because so much of model behavior is not governed by the harness – the code that wraps the model.
"A lot of decisions that I built into OpenClaw early on now can change because the models are so much better," he said.
Even if risks like prompt injection have been reduced through engineering efforts, Steinberger said, "you might not want to give your agent all the permissions."
Instead, he suggested using an agent to authorize your agent.

"You want to have another agent that can give it permissions or not and then this agent has to negotiate with another agent," he said. c91866ae59011088: Why use your smartphone when AI can do it for you? We’ve reached a new level of AI inanity with the launch of Opposable, a tool that taps, swipes, and types on Android phones and controls iPhones through a companion computer, sparing users the apparent burden of operating their own devices.

If you don't want to update a calendar event, start a timer, or enable dark mode, you can apparently use an AI agent app on your computer (any client that supports MCP will do) to have Opposable do the thing for you on a connected phone.
You could just do it on your computer, of course, but that’d require actually using your hands - like it’s some sort of baby’s toy. Lame.

Opposable describes the purpose of its app as being to “give your AI thumbs” that allow an agent to open apps, read the screen, tap, and type, all while signed in to a device as the person too lazy to use a super-convenient technology themselves.

As described in a blog post published by its creators Wednesday, Opposable's developers explain that its Android implementation uses accessibility services to inspect the screen, while screenshots provide visual input for an AI model. The model then decodes the images and figures out where it needs to tap on the screen in order to do whatever its user asked of it.

The visual processing is handled by a vision-language model known as GUI-Owl 1.5 2B, running through llama.cpp, while tasks can be handled by either a paired desktop AI agent or an on-device agent that works without a desktop connection (the latter is available only on Android devices – iPhones require a companion computer, with a Mac beta available and a hardware-assisted Windows/Linux option also advertised).
Even then, AI isn’t used for everything, with around 40 common tasks (setting an alarm, sending a text, switching Wi-Fi on or off) running as fixed code without an AI model involved.

Opposable doesn’t appear to be particularly fast, however, and its accuracy is questionable too. Opposable’s website includes three different examples of tasks executed using its product, and none seem to merit using an AI over, you know, human hands.

In one example, Claude Code over MCP is used to change the system’s theme to dark mode and then set a five-minute timer. This takes 50 seconds and requires 17 tool calls. In a second example using Claude Code and MCP, Opposable is asked to look up when Apollo 11 launched and who was on board, which takes just shy of 2 minutes. The number of tool calls isn’t mentioned, but the run cost is $0.44, which seems ridiculous when you can use your hands and figure it out for free. Hell, just asking Gemini or Siri right on a smartphone would return the answer faster and cheaper.
Those half-a-buck requests to Opposable could add up pretty quickly if you’re lazy enough to justify its use.

A third example shows a virtual Android device operating without a paired desktop agent, instead relying on the on-device agent that Opposable installs on Android phones. Opening the clock app and switching to the stopwatch tab takes it about 96 seconds, which is supposed to be impressive, apparently, as the company behind Opposable decided to showcase it on the thing’s website.
As for Opposable’s ability to actually accomplish tasks, well, that’s not exactly a sure thing.

“On eight tasks the model had never been tuned on, run on the emulator twice each, giving it the whole task succeeded 4 and 3 times,” the blog post notes. I’m pretty sure my brain and hands can do better without burning tokens to fail.

“Giving it one subgoal at a time and checking each claimed success against the accessibility tree before the next subgoal succeeded 6 times in both rounds,” the blog continues - so even when it gets babysat each step of the way, it still only succeeds at three-quarters of tasks. Cool - that’s really going to free up all that time wasted setting timers and doing other mundane tasks on my handset.

Why someone would install this on their Android device - which requires sideloading an APK and manually granting access to read and interact with the screen through accessibility settings - seems like a bit of a mystery. Opposable’s website even warns that it could be a security disaster: “whoever holds the token can operate the phone, so treat it like a password,” but still invites users to try.

An argument could be made for using Opposable as an accessibility tool for people with difficulty using a smartphone, but this isn’t mentioned anywhere on its website. Opposable is instead billed as a way to “hand off the phone chores,” leaving users free to do something else - just not on the phone currently being slowly controlled by a clumsy AI.
Sure, you could give your AI some virtual thumbs through Opposable, but … why? We reached out to the Opposable team to get an answer to that question, but didn’t hear back. ®

4b8e960bba5ff9c2: Nvidia hopes to capitalize on European sovereign AI demand by unloading a slew of new open weights models spanning chatbots, healthcare, and robotics.

The major model devs have the resources to build highly capable models from scratch. But most enterprises don't, and have instead been forced to fine tune open weights models from the likes of Mistral or H Company using their own datasets.
At GTC Berlin, Nvidia unveiled its latest additions to its open weights model library with refreshed Nemotron Retriever embedding and Alpamayo autonomous vehicle models.

While by no means the sexiest subclass of models out there, embedding models are some of the more useful ones for enterprise apps. Retrieval augmented generation (RAG), a technology we've explored extensively in the past, relies heavily on the embeddings generated by these models for applications like AI-augmented search.

At a high level, RAG works by cutting up documentation in chunks, then converting those into vectors called embeddings. The embeddings are then ranked based on their relevance to the user's query before they're fed into an LLM's context.

Nvidia's latest embedding and reranking models, based on Nemotron 3.5, support embeddings of both images and text across 34 languages. This time around, the models are being offered in sizes ranging from one to eight billion parameters, with NVFP4-quantized versions for those running on new Blackwell-based accelerators. That's small enough to run on something like a DGX Spark with plenty of room to spare for other models.

Always take vendor claims with the usual grain of salt, but among competing embedding models, Nvidia boasts that at BF16-precision, its new 8 billion parameter embedding and reranking models are now the top-ranked dense models on the ViDoRe V3.1 benchmarks.

However, not all documents are easily converted into embeddings. PDFs are notoriously difficult for embedding models to make sense of. They're often scanned from printed source material and formatted for consumption, which means scraping text and parsing charts. For this, Nvidia has also launched a refreshed Nemotron Parse model that's been trained specifically to extract information from PDF documents.
Nvidia claims the model can process roughly 10.5 pages a second when running the one billion-parameter model on a single H100.

Alongside the new embedding models, Nvidia is also rolling out access to Alpamayo 2 Edge, a more compact version of its autonomous driving model based on which promises real-time processing of streaming video and sensor data when running on the company's DRIVE AGX Thor platform.

The models come just a week after the GPU giant launched its Nemotron 3.5 Super vision language (VL) model and teased Nemotron 3.5 Bolt, a 74 billion-parameter mixture of experts (MoE) model designed to fit in as little as 24 GB of video memory. That model, Nvidia says, will be available for download starting Friday.

While open models provide enterprises and governments a path toward sovereign AI, Nvidia's models are somewhat unique in how they're released. Most open weights models are a sort of black box. Anyone can download them, but the data and processes used to arrive at those weights is a mystery. This isn't the case with many of Nvidia's models: Alongside their weights, Nvidia routinely releases the training data and the recipes used to turn it into the final model.

This means customers can not only inspect the model at a low level, but build a fully custom model based on Nvidia's Nemotron architecture, rather than trying to modify the weights after the fact through fine tuning. We should note that Nvidia is not the only one to do this. The Allen Institute has employed a similar strategy with its OLMo models for this very reason. ®

010aa00becaf980e: Unknown crims compromised LiteLLM's release process on Wednesday, distributing a malicious version (1.107.0) containing malware designed to steal cloud and AI credentials and a remote access trojan (RAT) capable of executing arbitrary code on infected machines through PyPI and Docker registries.

PyPI quarantined the trojanized version of the popular open source AI gateway within hours, and the Docker image (litellm/litellm:1.107.0) was removed from both Docker Hub and GHCR soon after - but anyone who ran the compromised package on any platform should assume their secrets have been stolen.

“Check for /tmp/.pc_once_* (the exfil has already fired if this file exists) and /tmp/remote_code_loader.lock (the C2 daemon ran or is still running if this file exists),” advised Aikido Security malware hunter Ilyas Makari. “The same applies to anyone who ran the official Docker image litellm/litellm:1.107.0, or pulled it via the latest, main-latest, or main-stable tags.”
The most recent safe version is v1.106.2.

While it’s too early to tell the scale of this latest LiteLLM supply chain attack – an earlier LiteLLM compromise in March potentially exposed more than 2,500 organizations and 434,000 CI/CD pipelines worldwide, according to CloudSEK – make sure to take these measures seriously, and check environments for any indicators of compromise.

Aikido, Google’s Wiz cloud security biz, and supply-chain security provider Socket have all published extensive threat-hunting and mitigation instructions for LiteLLM users and security teams, so give those a read stat.

LiteLLM, developed by BerriAI, provides a common interface for LLM providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Gemini, and receives about 23 million weekly downloads. This means a compromised installation can run alongside LLM provider API keys, cloud identities, and database connection strings - and expose a ton of valuable credentials, secrets, and other sensitive data to whoever uploaded the malicious package.
“Teams using 1.107.0 should stop deploying it and investigate environments where Python ran after installation, including proxy containers and CI runners,” Socket researchers said on Wednesday.

The malicious version was uploaded at 11:39 UTC, and according to Wiz kids Benjamin Read and Rami McCarthy, the payload originates with malicious commits made on github.com/Berri-AI/litellm, which is a hyphenated variant of the legitimate BerriAI organization.

Miscreants used this repo to inject the three malicious files into the LiteLLM release pipeline. These, according to Makari, include cook.pth, which causes the second file, cook.py, to run automatically every time Python is invoked on the machine, without any additional user action.

Meanwhile, cook.py contains the infostealer, and the third file, sitecustomize.py, is the RAT. Python also executes the RAT at interpreter startup, and this file spawns a background daemon that polls the attacker's infrastructure every hour for new commands to execute.
Upon executing, the infostealer harvests a ton of sensitive data across 16 modules targeting browsers, cloud providers, and AI services, according to Read and McCarthy.

It steals browser credentials and cookies from Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari, along with AWS credentials from ~/.aws/, environment variables, and EC2/ECS instance metadata (IMDS). It also collects users’ Google Cloud Platform service account keys and application default credentials, along with Microsoft Azure tokens from the CLI cache.
And then it also swipes API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and other LLM providers, plus SSH private keys, GPG keys, and shell history files.

The malware then encrypts all of this stolen data using AES-256-CBC, wraps the encryption key with an RSA-4096 public key, and sends the encrypted data via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled domain: http://www[.]litellm[.]dev/healthcheck.
BerriAI did not respond to The Register’s inquiries. This is an emerging story, and we will continue to update it as we learn more details.®

There is so much going on that is hopeful: biodiversity tracking, river protection, rewilding. Shruti Suresh, from the independent watchdog Global Witness, told those in attendance that if they wanted to effect change, they should protest against Jackdaw and the Rosebank oilfield project. The message was so well understood that it didn’t need labouring. The mood in the room when the news came in was one of audible dismay. People had just watched the minister for climate transition declare that she could see the challenges ahead and was ready for them. The Jackdaw announcement will face immediate protest and legal challenge, but it sends a very clear signal from the government: we don’t mean what we say about ending emissions. 7ae486925b0f5ddc: Make sure you don’t say anything mean or secret after hanging up a call on Signal, as a bug in the encrypted messaging app’s calling library could prevent a call from ending properly, potentially leaving audio and possibly video active.

The vulnerability, CVE-2026-113380, was published by MITRE on Tuesday and given a CVSS score of 9.3, marking it as a critical issue in Signal’s open-source RingRTC library in every single version before 2.72.0. That update was pushed out last month, but the vulnerability wasn’t made public until now.

RingRTC is Signal’s own calling library built on top of WebRTC, a technology introduced in 2011 that has since become widely used for voice and video communication over the internet. RingRTC provides Signal-specific calling functionality using WebRTC, which already encrypts media traffic, but that isn't stopping RingRTC from failing to hang up calls in certain conditions, according to the CVE report.

What’s happening is, in essence, a denial-of-service attack on RingRTC’s finite state machine (FSM) event queue, which handles events involved in managing calls. If one of the people on the call saturates the FSM queue with requests, it can become overwhelmed and fail to process a hangup request, preventing the call from terminating properly. The vulnerability is classified as CWE-754, or improper checking for unusual or exceptional conditions, according to a report posted to GitHub.
A conceptual proof of concept is available in the GitHub report linked above, using a Python script to simulate how flooding an event queue can prevent a hangup request from being processed.
Were a malicious actor to exploit this, the person on the other end may think the call has been terminated, but either or both of their video and audio channels could still be open.

The attack complexity is considered low according to the CVE, and while CISA’s known exploited vulnerabilities catalog doesn’t indicate this has been spotted in the wild, Signal users ought to ensure they’ve updated their apps - mobile and desktop - to the latest versions to ensure they don’t end up being caught on a hot mic without any notice.

Comparing RingRTC 2.72.0 to the previous version indicates that Signal's fix allows the call's finite state machine (FSM) to detect termination requests independently of the event queue, while adding a timeout to prevent stalled processing from indefinitely blocking a hangup.

It's not entirely clear from Signal's release notes when the fixed version of RingRTC reached the Android, iOS, and desktop versions of its apps. Signal Desktop's release history indicates that RingRTC 2.72.0 was incorporated in September, but the precise rollout dates across all platforms remain unclear. We’ve reached out to Signal to learn more, but haven’t heard back.
In the meantime, best to update your installation to be sure you’re not still vulnerable. That, and watch what you say after hanging up a call. ®

5fc05b0f30bad9e1: In its current iteration, SpaceX is largely a data company seeking to provide enormous amounts of compute for artificial intelligence. During an earnings call on Tuesday afternoon, company officials spent much of their time discussing ambitious plans to roll out up to 10 GW of compute in 2027—on the ground.

Gone are the days of aspirational talk about sending humans to Mars and settling the red planet. Now it is almost all about artificial intelligence and the data needed to support its expansion. However, the company's long-term ambitions to provide data services from space, initially with the Starlink Internet constellation and eventually through the "Starmind" data center constellation, still rely on an actual rocket.

That would be the Starship vehicle, and during the earnings call, SpaceX founder Elon Musk and the company's president and chief operating officer, Gwynne Shotwell, provided new performance targets for the vehicle.
61ce8fd1c476c25f: RAMALLAH: Israeli forces on Wednesday briefly detained a US congressional candidate as he joined activists supporting Palestinians harvesting olives in the face of threats by extremist settlers.

Brad Lander, a left-wing Democrat who is expected to easily win a House seat in New York City on Nov 3, posted on social media that he was detained along with a group of rabbis and volunteers as they harvested olives west of Bethlehem in the occupied West Bank.
"The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn't a crime under any law I know," Lander wrote on X.
He later wrote that he was released on account of his prominence, adding that "Palestinians face far worse consequences every day."
The Israeli foreign ministry lashed out at Lander over what it called a "calculated political stunt", and said he had ignored guidance to coordinate with Israeli authorities.
"This was not about harvesting olives. It was about harvesting headlines," it said.
The Israeli military said that the Palestinian landowner had not requested permission to conduct the harvest.
"This coordination is necessary to ensure the security of the area and maintain public order," it said, pointing to the "security risk of an uncoordinated harvest" near an Israeli settlement.
Israel has faced growing international criticism over violence during the harvest, with rights groups documenting multiple attacks and other disruptions each day by settlers against Palestinians.
Israel on Monday announced it had made several arrests after settlers beat up a US photojournalist covering the incidents and a French mayor who had come for the olive season.
The violence comes in the final days before Israeli elections in which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has sought to shore up his right-wing base, which is staunchly pro-settlement.
Israel has come under growing fire within the United States, traditionally its top ally.
Lander, who is Jewish, is a close ally of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, an outspoken critic of Israeli policies.
In a party primary in June, Lander ousted the sitting congressman, Dan Goldman, one of a dwindling number of Democrats who support Israel.--AFP
2f7554dfc8afedca: AUSTRALIA'S security chiefs had warned of "online echo chambers" fuelling grievances and conspiracies and stepped up prosecutions for threats of political violence ahead of Monday's attack on a lawmaker in a rural town.

Independent lawmaker Helen Haines, 65, underwent surgery overnight but remains in a critical condition after being struck deliberately by a car in an attack that "does shake all of us", Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Tuesday.
Broadcaster ABC and the Sydney Morning Herald reported she had lost a leg.
Brendan Nugent, 43, is in custody after Haines was hit outside her office in Wangaratta, just over 200km northeast of Melbourne.

Police have charged Nugent with dangerous driving causing serious injury and intentionally causing serious injury, as well as the federal crime of harming a public official, which carries a penalty of 10 years in prison.
Police described it as an isolated incident with the motive under investigation by the counter-terrorism team.

Acts of political violence are rare in Australia, and Albanese told the national broadcaster he wanted the country to remain a place where lawmakers can engage with people, go shopping and watch football.
But he said security needed to be "dealt with" amid a significant increase in threats.
Australia's Human Rights Commission said the attack happened "against a backdrop of increasing polarisation and threats against politicians", which could undermine democracy.
Threats against Australian lawmakers and electorate offices doubled between 2021 and last year, with 1,067 incidents reported to police last year.

The Australian Federal Police formed a National Security Investigations team last October, described by police commissioner Krissy Barrett as a "flying squad of hate disruptors", resulting in 41 people being charged for threats against federal politicians, ministers and the prime minister.
Just this month, three men were charged over separate threats to politicians and government officials, and another three were sentenced by courts.

The nation's spy chief, Australian Security Intelligence Organisation director-general Mike Burgess, said last year politically motivated violence was among the agency's fastest growing security concerns, driven by "griev-ance narratives, conspiracies and online echo chambers".
Political intolerance, violent rhetoric and polarisation were also contributing to a "permissive environment of violence", Burg-ess said on Tuesday.
The lawmakers targeted are across the political spectrum and include men.
But the nature of threats directed at female lawmakers is "particularly troubling" because they are targeted because they are women, the federal police said last year.
The University of Melbourne's associate head of psychological sciences, Lisa Phillips, said she was not surprised it was a female lawmaker who had been attacked.
Victoria's state Parliament commissioned Phillips to survey lawmakers on online abuse and stalking five years ago.

"The female politicians who responded almost ubiquitously reported experiences of either unwanted approaches, persistent unwanted contact from people, or experiences of threats or of assault," she said.
Eighty-five per cent of the threats received by the Victorian women lawmakers were gender-based abuse, the study found.
The attack on Haines may not be linked to federal politics, Phillips added.
"If you have a grievance against the system, you don't care which part of the system you are targeting."

9aa86826f7db40ab: PORT DICKSON: A final-year college student undergoing practical training at a hotel in Lukut was found dead behind an eatery here yesterday.

8cd2818168e33eb9: DIMONA: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday that the only way to remove the threat posed by Iran was to topple its government.

"Iran wanted to destroy us; we stopped them. They wanted to produce nuclear bombs; we stopped them... Yet they persist," he said during an election rally in the southern town of Dimona. "Therefore, there is only one way to end this: by toppling this regime."
"This is the directive I have issued to the Israel Defence Forces, to the Mossad, and to all our security branches," he added, without specifying when or how that directive would be executed.
The sabre-rattling came as the premier headed into the last week of a tight race for re-election.

Netanyahu had instructed the Israeli military to plan for resumed strikes against Iran earlier this month, according to sources cited by the Financial Times on Wednesday, but US President Donald Trump reportedly objected to the idea.
The US leader has publicly said that he does not intend to restart the war, which Washington started in February alongside Israel, before the US mid-term elections early next month.
This week, Netanyahu thanked Trump in a video for his endorsement in the Israeli election, and said that the two leaders have "a job to finish" in Iran.
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz also warned against a potential threat from Iran.

Speaking at an officers' graduation ceremony in southern Israel on Wednesday, he said that "the Iranian regime is at its weakest point ever, and we recognise that this weakness could lead it to take the most extreme steps."
"If Iran attacks Israel, Iran will burn!" he said.
Katz also warned against unspecified attempts by Israel's enemies to disrupt the upcoming vote.
"In recent days, we have identified attempts by our enemies – led by Iran and its proxies – to advance attacks that could affect the outcome of Israel's elections," he said. --AFP
5451747272347677: FOR nearly two years, United States President Donald Trump's heavy-handed deportation drive has sowed fear in immigrant communities and created a flood of grim headlines and social media videos.
Now, with midterm elections looming, many Latino voters who helped propel Trump and his Republican Party to power in 2024 say they are fed up.

In southern Florida's Doral, a mostly Latino community near Miami that is also home to one of Trump's golf clubs, residents said that worries about potential raids have left businesses without staff and classrooms with fewer pupils.
Known as "Doralzuela", the area is home to a large Venezuelan population and could be a bellwether for whiplashing Latino sentiment nationwide.
"I feel sad and disappointed," said restaurant-owner Maria Fernanda Perez. "My thinking was that the economy would improve," the 32-year-old said of her vote for Trump.
Three of her employees stopp-ed showing up over fears of being deported, she said, with sales falling 40 per cent as people in the community pull back from going out.
"My whole family, all my friends, are going through immigration proceedings, and they're no longer working, they're no longer going about their daily lives."
Trump campaigned on promises of a historic deportation drive, but emphasised the targeting of hardened criminals.
With over a thousand people being taken into immigration custody every day, many Latino voters feel misled.
Like other communities around the country, residents in Doral have begun exchanging messages to alert one another to the presence of immigration agents or to someone being detained.

A New York Times and Siena College poll conducted last month showed 66 per cent of Hispanic respondents disapproved of Trump's performance, and 78 per cent said they would prefer that Democrats take control of Congress from Republicans.
Perez declined to say how she would vote in the upcoming election, but said emphatically: "Anyone but Trump".
Carlos Bermudez, a lawyer of Venezuelan origin, receives constant calls from desperate people going through immigration proceedings.
"They don't go out, they can't go to work. It's constant psychological pressure, and it affects the whole community," said the 47-year-old.
Bermudez, who describes himself as a Republican, expressed concerns about the party's "extreme" positions.

"I'm a Republican because I come from a country where communism, socialism took hold, and I don't want to continue with that ideology, but I don't agree with what the extreme wing of the party is doing now," he said.
Doral Councilman Rafael Pineyro said: "There's uncertainty, there's fear... It's not just Doral, it's the whole Latino community in South Florida that's affected."
Pineyro, a Republican, also questioned the Trump administration's immigration strategy.
"This isn't right, because this isn't what was promised in 2024 when we were talking about (deporting) criminals," he said.
Trump's policies could hamper gains made by Republicans in recent years among Florida's Cuban, Venezuelan and other Latino voters, he warned.
"That opportunity has been slipping away more and more in recent months because of bad decisions, in my view, specifically when it comes to the economy and immigration."

d06e6f0b4cb69fd8: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will upgrade baggage and body scanners at all international entry points in phases to strengthen security screening, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said.
In a written reply published on the Parliament website, he said the upgrades would introduce next-generation scanning technology integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) analytics.

He was responding to Rodiyah Sapiee (GPS-Batang Sadong), who asked about weaknesses identified in security screening systems and immediate measures to prevent syndicates from abusing special access lanes for aviation personnel, following the arrest of a Malaysian pilot in Jakarta for carrying drugs.

Saifuddin said existing baggage scanners at Kuala Lumpur International Airport's (KLIA) departure lanes and airports nationwide complied with International Civil Aviation Organization standards, which focus on detecting explosives, weapons and dangerous metal objects to ensure flight safety.

"The existing baggage scanners at KLIA's departure lanes and airports nationwide are not equipped with technology to detect contraband such as drugs. Detection depends on the expertise, visual awareness and risk-profile analysis of screening personnel," he said.
He added that security screening at airports was also supported by intelligence from security agencies to curb smuggling through the country's entry points.

Saifuddin said a joint ministerial memorandum between the Home Ministry and the Transport Ministry, approved by the cabinet on Aug 19, 2026, endorsed an action plan to improve and mitigate security risks at the country's entry points, comprising 17 substantive recommendations.

The plan covers three main areas: aviation security, national and border security, and physical security and protection. Implementation will be phased, with short-term measures taking zero to six months, medium-term measures six to 24 months, and long-term measures more than 24 months.

To address the risk of aviation and airport personnel abusing special access lanes, the government and relevant agencies will tighten security screening for airport security pass applications and renewals.
Saifuddin said the measures included strengthening the e-Vetting system to prevent individuals deemed to pose a risk from being granted access to restricted areas.

The government would also introduce regular job rotations for personnel working in restricted security areas to reduce the risk of collusion and manipulation of controls at special access lanes, he said.
cbedbd3df6a4bb3a: WASHINGTON: Government agencies and companies around the world shut down websites Wednesday after two critical flaws came to light involving PHP, a programming language that is the basis for a large share of the internet.
The US National Security Agency told organizations to patch immediately or pull vulnerable systems offline.
The flaws "often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database," the NSA said in a statement on X.
Attackers could use them to take over web servers without needing a password.
PHP sits underneath popular web design platforms so the weaknesses potentially affect a vast range of websites, from online stores and news outlets to government services.

The discovery came amid a surge in software security disclosures driven by increasingly powerful AI models, with the number of vulnerabilities found in 2026 on track to roughly double last year's record total.
PHP volunteers released a fix on Wednesday.
"If you run PHP, it is imperative that you update now," the PHP Foundation, which funds developers working on the language, said in a blog post.

The flaws were reported in August by security firm Calif and by ChatGPT maker OpenAI, which flagged them independently on the same day. Google-owned cloud security company Wiz later reported further ways to exploit them.
The flaws had been reported privately to PHP's developers at the time and kept confidential while a fix was prepared.
Details leaked online Tuesday, a day before the planned release, prompting the rush to take sites offline.

In France, local government websites, including the Paris Police Prefecture, have been inaccessible since Wednesday afternoon at the request of the French National Cybersecurity Agency, following "detection of a critical security vulnerability," the Ministry of the Interior said.

In the Netherlands, the national digital identity service DigiD, the website of the House of Representatives and the site of the national cybersecurity center went offline as a precaution, according to Dutch public broadcaster NOS.
Belgium's foreign ministry temporarily took its websites offline as a precaution, it said on X, although the Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium had recorded no attacks on Belgian sites.-AFP
fb13de5b854a09a8: PETALING JAYA: Sebanyak 13,072 jawatan doktor di Kementerian Kesihatan (KKM) masih kosong setakat 30 Jun lalu, yang merangkumi 1,660 jawatan pakar dan 11,412 jawatan bukan pakar, kata Menteri Kesihatan, Dzulkefly Ahmad.
Beliau berkata, seramai 3,510 pegawai perubatan meletak jawatan antara 2024 hingga 2026, termasuk 1,252 doktor lantikan tetap dan 2,258 doktor kontrak.
Daripada jumlah yang meletak jawatan itu, 51.4% beralih ke sektor swasta, 36.8% atas sebab peribadi dan 4.5% menyertai badan berkanun.
Sebanyak 2.9% lagi bekerja atau menetap di luar negara, 2.6% meletak jawatan kerana masalah kesihatan, 1.5% melanjutkan pelajaran dan 0.3% membuka klinik sendiri.
Beliau turut memaklumkan lapan pakar perubatan meletak jawatan atau berhijrah ke luar negara.

Dzulkefly berkata demikian dalam jawapan bertulis di Parlimen bagi menjawab soalan V Ganabatirau (PH-Klang) berhubung doktor yang meletak jawatan atau berhijrah ke luar negara, kekosongan jawatan, kekurangan doktor pakar, tempoh menunggu penempatan latihan siswazah perubatan (housemanship) serta keberkesanan langkah mengekalkan doktor dalam perkhidmatan kesihatan awam.
Beliau berkata, KKM telah melantik 14,064 pegawai perubatan tetap dan 9,847 pegawai perubatan kontrak dalam tempoh sama.
Bagi menangani kekurangan tenaga kerja, jelasnya, seramai 4,500 doktor kontrak ditawarkan pelantikan tetap tahun ini.

Menurutnya, sebuah pasukan petugas yang ditubuhkan Jabatan Perkhidmatan Awam pada April lalu sedang meneliti isu berkaitan tenaga kerja, manakala KKM diberikan mandat untuk mengurus dan mengagihkan jawatan diluluskan bagi mempercepatkan proses pengambilan kakitangan.

Dzulkefly berkata, enam hospital kerajaan mencapai sasaran merawat sekurang-kurangnya 70% pesakit bukan kecemasan dalam tempoh dua jam, berbanding purata tempoh menunggu sebelum ini empat hingga enam jam.

Dalam jawapan bertulis kepada Dr Zulkafperi Hanapi (Bebas-Tanjong Karang), katanya, Hospital Raja Permaisuri Bainun di Ipoh mencatatkan kadar tertinggi, dengan 98.61% pesakit zon hijau dirawat dalam tempoh dua jam.
Ini diikuti Hospital Ampang (88.78%), Hospital Selayang (74.1%), Hospital Sultanah Aminah di Johor Bahru (73.2%), Hospital Tengku Ampuan Rahimah di Klang (72.2%) dan Hospital Kuala Lumpur (71.8%).
Beliau turut memaklumkan penurunan 9% kehadiran pesakit di enam hospital utama susulan lanjutan waktu operasi di klinik kesihatan kerajaan terpilih.
Klinik itu beroperasi sehingga 9 malam pada hari bekerja serta dari 8 pagi hingga 1 tengah hari pada hujung minggu dan cuti umum.
Jelasnya, lanjutan waktu operasi itu membantu mengalihkan pesakit mengalami masalah kesihatan ringan daripada jabatan kecemasan hospital.
Dzulkefly turut berkata, semua lapan inisiatif di bawah pasukan petugas khas reformasi agensi bagi mengurangkan kesesakan pesakit di hospital, telah dilaksanakan sepenuhnya setakat Jun lalu.

Langkah lain termasuk penyumberluaran rawatan kepada pengamal perubatan am swasta, peluasan saringan digital bagi pesakit bukan kecemasan sebelum mereka ke klinik (meliputi 545 klinik kesihatan) serta penambahbaikan aliran pesakit di hospital kerajaan.
05b99ea8d320d9c0: ALEKSA Simic, a political science student at Belgrade University, did not hesitate when he learned that the collapse of a railway station canopy in the northern Serbian city of Novi Sad had killed 16 people in November 2024.

Demanding justice for the dead, and an end to the kind of corruption that many believed led to the station's shoddy construction, he and other students blockaded the political science faculty in protest.
As Serbia mourned, sympathetic residents brought them homemade meals, mattresses and pillows. Many stopped by to discuss the students' demands.
"For the first time, I had a sense of belonging to a community. I realised that my voice mattered," Simic said.

Two years on, as Serbia prepares for elections on Oct 25, the student protest movement has ballooned to become one of the most powerful political forces in the country and poses the greatest threat yet to the rule of Aleksandar Vucic, who has dominated Serbian politics first as prime minister, then president, since 2014.

With protests raging in cities across Europe, fuelled by the high cost of living, a shortage of jobs and poor education standards, the Serbian students have shown what a force younger generations can be when they harness widespread discontent.

In interviews with Reuters, a dozen students and teachers described how a methodical countrywide door-knocking campaign, peaceful marches, a tightly controlled media message and a constant rotation of leaders to protect individuals from government smear campaigns have helped maintain momentum in Serbia.
Now, they have their own "Students Win" list of 250 candidates for Sunday's election, which includes university professors, actors, farmers and even a popular rapper.

The only poll published this month, by New Serbian Political Thought (NSPM) on Oct 20, showed the students' list of candidates edging ahead of Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) with 44.5 per cent of the vote to 42.7 per cent, although betting odds favour Vucic.
"The protests changed the society. It showed people they are not alone," said Florian Bieber, professor of Southeast European history and politics at the University of Graz.
The big question is how the students would govern should they win on Sunday.

Vucic is a significant international figure, managing a delicate balancing act that seeks closer ties with China, a major investor, and Russia, Serbia's traditional ally and principal supplier of natural gas, while leaving the door open to joining the European Union even with the accession process stalled.
The students' list is headed by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, although they have said this does not mean he would become prime minister should they win.

Some political analysts wonder how the country would fare on the international stage with an unknown at the helm, while there are scant details about how the students will set about fulfilling their pledges to fight corruption, promote transparency, create greater media freedom and enact education reform at home.

Critics also point to their silence on joining the EU and relations with the former province of Kosovo. Pro-European opponents of Vucic's government criticise them for saying that they would not introduce sanctions on Russia.

"A (student-led) government would pursue broad reforms to tackle corruption, overhaul key public institutions and companies, and dismantle patronage networks," consultancy Teneo said in an analyst note on Tuesday.
"However, strong bureaucratic resistance could generate short-term institutional instability."
Vucic, 56, stepped down as president in September to run again for prime minister in the snap election.

While he has overseen a period of strong economic growth and a fall in unemployment, critics blame him for democratic backsliding, the silencing of critics and the media, and hampering Serbia's EU accession by not undertaking necessary reforms.
Police have beaten protesters and threatened people who voice opposition online, rights groups, activists and students told Reuters.
Simmering anger towards the government boiled over with the collapse of the station roof in Novi Sad.

Vucic has sought to discredit the student movement, saying it is trying to destroy Serbia and accusing foreign agents from Croatia and Montenegro of financing it, but that has not dented their support.

Vucic and the authorities have repeatedly denied the allegations of corruption and violence and attempts to discredit the opposition. The students dismiss claims that they are being organised from abroad.
The student protests were small to begin with: days after the canopy collapse, a few dozen people blocked traffic in Novi Sad and Belgrade for one minute for each person who was killed.

Less than three months later, in late January 2025, then prime minister and close Vucic ally Milos Vucevic resigned a day after tens of thousands of people blocked one of Belgrade's main junctions, joined by farmers in their tractors.
In March that year, the students led hundreds of thousands of people through Belgrade, the biggest anti-government march in a generation.
By then, the movement had a symbol: a red handprint, representing the blood that the protesters say is on the government's hands.
"We felt we had importance and that we had a greater responsibility," Simic said.
University faculties across the country held plenums and working groups focused on media and social media strategies, and organising marches.
On the first anniversary of the roof collapse, the students walked from Belgrade to Novi Sad. People in small villages offered fruit.

An image of a man with a traditional Serbian hat hugging a Muslim student in a headscarf flooded social media - which supporters hailed as an emblem of a young, progressive Serbia after the devastating Balkan wars of the 1990s.
Ahead of Sunday's vote, student groups have undergone training on election fraud and say teams plan to be present at polling stations.

Gavrilo Andric was a software engineer for a big company when the protests began. An amateur photographer, he watched the movement grow, eventually leaving his job to become its unofficial documenter.
"I finally realised that in our society we have a group of people who see things can be improved and want to work on it together with other people," he told Reuters.
