d0b4238639f98149: KUALA LUMPUR: "This is not Malaysia versus Indonesia. Our flags are different, but when we struggle to breathe, the suffering is the same," said Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman.
He was responding to criticism by former Indonesian trade minister Muhammad Lutfi over his call for Asean to boycott Indonesia over recurring transboundary haze.
Syed Saddiq said the issue should not be viewed as a dispute between the two countries, but addressed through evidence-based action against any party found responsible for environmental pollution.
He said companies from Malaysia, Indonesia or Singapore proven to have burned forests for profit should face action under Indonesian law.

"I will not protect polluters, even if they are from my own country. Do not choose sides based on whether a company is Malaysian, Indonesian or Singaporean. If they are proven to have burned forests for quick profits, take action," he said in a video posted on social media today.
Syed Saddiq also said large-scale plantation ownership alone was not proof of a company's involvement in forest fires.

On SG Guthrie, he claimed there was no evidence so far that the company had caused the fires. He said it had 67 teams comprising more than 1,000 trained personnel, drones and infrared equipment to tackle the problem, at a cost of more than RM800,000 a month.
He also cited a Greenpeace report, saying it recorded 19 haze source points in KLK's concessions compared with 6,811 others.
Syed Saddiq said Malaysia had offered assistance to tackle forest fires in Indonesia, including aircraft, three helicopters and personnel, but claimed the offer had received no response.

Lutfi was reported to have criticised Syed Saddiq's call for an Asean boycott, saying the haze crisis should not be used for cheap political publicity. He also highlighted the Indonesian firefighters who had died tackling the fires and the hundreds of thousands of Indonesians exposed to the smoke.

Syed Saddiq had made the boycott proposal while debating the 2027 Budget, calling for Asean countries to take action against the recurring haze, including cutting funding to companies linked to open burning and encouraging consumers to pressure businesses involved.
"You must treat them as parties to be boycotted in this region," he said.
ca8c9116993ac56d: EXPRESS bus associations have clashed once more with the Transport Ministry, a recurring cycle for two decades.
Historically, they have been structural conflicts, as the government pushes for centralised regulation but operators struggle for financial stability and operational flexibility.
Previously, the two locked horns over the regulated fare structure.

The Pan Malaysian Bus Operators Association demanded a hike in ceiling fares, citing soaring operational costs, inflation and higher spending on vehicle maintenance. But the ministry insisted on regulating economy fares though temporary concessions during peak periods.
Consequently, operators reduced the number of standard economy buses and turned to "unregulated" executive or VIP ones at uncapped ticket prices.
There has been no development yet on moves to liberalise economy fares for a "win-win" policy that balances safety, service quality and profitability with passenger burdens.

Last year, another clash erupted. The Land Public Transport Agency (Apad) ordered buses to transition to Terminal Bersepadu Selatan to weed out ticket touts. It meant that picking up passengers directly from hotels or malls would incur penalties.

Associations countered that the Apad move, on top of charging hefty terminal facility fees, squeezes already thin profit margins. In the latest clash, Apad ordered that express bus tickets be sold only through licensed terminals from Nov 1.

Previously, passengers purchased tickets from terminals, online ticketing agents or operators' websites. Operators are aghast at giving up their sales options but the ministry's rationale is that it wants to curb unauthorised ticket sales and bring order to a chaotic industry.
The new system aims to reduce confusion, disputes and the risk of falling victim to unscrupulous ticket sellers.
Many online travel agencies are also based overseas, making it difficult to intervene after service failures, cancellations or refund disputes.

The Apad system aims to reduce unnecessary costs and improve returns for operators. Still, these reforms must be implemented sensibly without dismissing operators' concerns, especially as they have invested heavily in their own online booking systems.
They also fear the new ticketing system may create a monopoly that raises overheads and slashes profit margins.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke has promised engagement with operators to clarify the new rules, including how they can still maintain their websites and other digital utilities.
Nevertheless, the ministry noted that operators, not passengers, still pay digital service charges while terminal operators cannot charge above existing rates.
While the operators' angst is understandable, they still face driver shortages and aging buses alongside high-profile accidents.
At the same time, streamlining ticket sales ensures better crowd control, efficient schedules and accountability.
00fa329140497c1a: DIMONA: Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday that the only way to remove the threat posed by Iran was to topple its government.

"Iran wanted to destroy us; we stopped them. They wanted to produce nuclear bombs; we stopped them... Yet they persist," he said during an election rally in the southern town of Dimona. "Therefore, there is only one way to end this: by toppling this regime."
"This is the directive I have issued to the Israel Defense Forces, to the Mossad, and to all our security branches," he added, without specifying when or how that directive would be executed.
The sabre-rattling came as the premier headed into the last week of a tight race for re-election.

Netanyahu had instructed the Israeli military to plan for resumed strikes against Iran earlier this month, according to sources cited by the Financial Times on Wednesday, but US President Donald Trump reportedly objected to the idea.
The US leader has publicly said that he does not intend to restart the war, which Washington started in February alongside Israel, before the US mid-term elections early next month.
This week, Netanyahu thanked Trump in a video for his endorsement in the Israeli election and said that the two leaders have "a job to finish" in Iran.
Israeli defence minister Israel Katz also warned against a potential threat from Iran.

Speaking at an officers' graduation ceremony in southern Israel on Wednesday, he said that "the Iranian regime is at its weakest point ever, and we recognise that this weakness could lead it to take the most extreme steps".
"If Iran attacks Israel, Iran will burn!" he said.
Katz also warned against unspecified attempts by Israel's enemies to disrupt the upcoming vote.
"In recent days, we have identified attempts by our enemies – led by Iran and its proxies – to advance attacks that could affect the outcome of Israel's elections," he said.
e9890a0f7286e589: OpenBSD 8.0 brings bigger virtual machines, graphics improvements, and another helping of AI mockery. The round version number doesn't signal a radical break with its predecessors.

OpenBSD 8.0 is the 61st release of the project. Developer Bryan Steele posted a highlights rundown on Mastodon. Wireless improvements include updates to the qwx driver for Qualcomm Wi-Fi 6 hardware. Its VMM/VMD hypervisor now supports multiprocessor VMs with up to 64 virtual CPUs in each guest.

The kernel virtual memory address space on x86-64 is now 512 GB, up from 4 GB, allowing for GPUs with large amounts of VRAM. On Arm64 machines, OpenBSD supports hibernation, and on both x86-64 and Arm64 it can use CPU AES instructions for faster encrypted swap.

Component upgrades include OpenSSH 10.6 and LibreSSL 4.4.0, and the DRM graphics driver stack from Linux 6.18. The default C compiler is Clang/LLVM 22, including for the SPARC64 edition – but at the cost of dropping support for the Loongson architecture.

The list of errata is short, with just four fixes – but then, version 8.0 is very new. Just days before this release, there was a high-profile OpenBSD issue: Calif's "Big Fish" research describes a decades-old shared-memory bug chained with a separate kernel flaw to gain local root access. Both were fixed in OpenBSD 7.9, through errata 026 and 018 respectively.

Project leader Theo de Raadt forked OpenBSD from NetBSD 1.0 in 1995, and the first release of the new OS was OpenBSD 1.2 in July 1996 – so version 8.0 is as close as the project will get to a 30th anniversary release. According to Calif's proof-of-concept code on GitHub, the bug was in the original code that both OpenBSD and NetBSD inherited from the original BSD codebase – which is how come there's a 37-year-old bug in a 30-year-old project. A HackerNews comment says: "Interestingly, looks like this was accidentally fixed in NetBSD during a rewrite of that code in August of 1999."
The project has not updated its infamous slogan. The homepage still proclaims: "Only two remote holes in the default install, in a heck of a long time!"

As we noted in May when OpenBSD 7.9 appeared, the project rejects code generated by LLMs, although on the basis of licensing concerns rather than its cousin NetBSD's explicit anti-AI stance. As we reported recently, this strict anti-AI stance seems to be serving NetBSD well.

OpenBSD is also an anti-AI project, and for this release, the website goes out of its way to make that very clear. OpenBSD's mascot is a pufferfish, and in the banner artwork for the new release, "Puffy" has an extra eye – and the signpost in the image's background also has malformed text, a hallmark of early image-generation bots. The eyes are also constantly blinking – one at a time – to emphasize that this is a reference to Blinky the mutant fish from The Simpsons. In case you missed The Simpsons reference, the version 8.0 release theme song makes it even more explicit: it's titled "The Simps on AI." The lyrics and the vocals parody both Simpsons characters and AI users. Our favorite line sounds like Grampa Simpson, and says:
Back in my day we didn't have artificial intelligence, we had real stupidity – and we liked it.

We've seen negative reactions online, but then we often find that some people lack much of a sense of humor. For our part, we really enjoyed seeing the OpenBSD team having such fun. We reckon it will appeal to many Butlerian Jihadi types. It certainly did to The Reg FOSS desk.
A little Wine with your pufferfish
A couple of days before the 8.0 release came an unexpected announcement on the openbsd-ports mailing list: a proposed port of Wine for OpenBSD.

This is a new version of the Wine 11 runtime that allows Windows binaries to launch and run on OpenBSD. This is a 64-bit version of Wine for OpenBSD on x86-64, and for now, this means it can only run 64-bit Windows code.

(For the technical nitty-gritty: Wine needs to manipulate the CPU's GS register. Windows on x86-64 uses the GS segment base to locate the Thread Environment Block (TEB), as the late great Geoff Chappell explained. This is a very longstanding Windows data structure, going all the way back through Windows 95 to OS/2. The port was particularly tricky because OpenBSD doesn't allow programs to alter that, so the port is emulating instructions that use the %gs segment override. The snags are that this means 32-bit code doesn't work, and secondly, because this is unnecessary on Linux, the code is unlikely to be merged back into upstream Wine.)

If you want to see it working, there are a few screenshot galleries on Reddit's openbsd_gaming group, showing a number of recent major titles running: Some samples from WIP wine port, more wine-on-OpenBSD screenshots, and even more wine-on-OpenBSD proof.

The port comes hedged with caveats, notable among them that Wine does not do any kind of sandboxing, so using it potentially opens up OpenBSD to Windows malware. However, for some users, this could be a very useful addition.

OpenBSD is the simplest and cleanest member of the BSD family, indeed, of the FOSS Unix family. Part of this is because entire subsystems are missing that the other BSDs provide. Bluetooth connections to Apple's wireless keyboards and pointing devices aren't supported. There's no logical volume management – which would massively help with OpenBSD's complex disk partitioning. There's no journaling filesystem either (although a port of the new Gefs is in progress). While small and clean, its priorities favor security and simplicity, though performance will depend on the hardware and workload.
Importantly – since you probably will need to ask for help – the OpenBSD community does not have a reputation for friendliness.

Saying that, it is quite a lot easier to get OpenBSD installed and running, complete with its 25-year-old version 2.2.5 of the Fvwm window manager, than either NetBSD or FreeBSD. If you're looking for an AI-free, and indeed systemd-free, path away from Linux, OpenBSD 8.0 is very definitely worth a try. ®
08fd9e9d10a029a3: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 72 Malaysians were detained overseas on suspicion of drug-related offences from January to Oct 15, with 1,704kg of drugs worth RM81.76 million seized.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said 48 cases were recorded, involving 57 men and 15 women.

Thailand recorded the highest number of arrests at 19, followed by Indonesia (16), Taiwan and Singapore (eight each), Japan (five), the Philippines (four), India and Hong Kong (three each), Macau (two), and South Korea, Nigeria, the Maldives and Sri Lanka (one each).
Hussein said international drug syndicates could be exploiting Malaysians as drug couriers through job offers, lucrative rewards, sponsored travel and requests to deliver goods for third parties.
"Such tactics could deceive individuals who are unaware of the risks and legal implications, exposing them to severe legal action in the countries concerned," he said in a statement.

Among the cases was the detention of five Malaysians at Haneda Airport in Tokyo on Oct 10 for allegedly attempting to smuggle about 5kg of cocaine worth RM3.1 million. Malaysians had also been detained in drug-related cases in Macau and Singapore.
Hussein said drug trafficking and smuggling could carry severe penalties, including the death penalty in some countries, depending on the offence, the quantity of drugs and the applicable laws.
He urged the public, particularly youths, students and those planning to travel overseas, to be wary of suspicious job offers, free travel and promises of lucrative rewards.
He also warned against carrying or handing over items for others without knowing their contents and purpose, as syndicates could exploit unsuspecting individuals as drug couriers. -- BERNAMA
ebe891935f169822: PETALING JAYA: The PAS-led Kelantan government has sidestepped calls to drop the sole Bersatu representative from the state executive council.
Deputy menteri besar Fadzli Hassan said the state government was closely following political developments at the federal and state levels.
"We will consider our options and choose the best approach," he told FMT.
Bersatu's sole exco member in Kelantan - Ayer Lanas assemblyman Kamaruddin Nor - oversees the tourism, arts, culture and heritage portfolio.
Wawasan vice-president Wan Saiful Wan Jan had called for the positions of Bersatu exco members in the PAS-led states of Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu to be reviewed.
This followed Perikatan Nasional's deregistration by the Registrar of Societies in response to a complaint filed by Bersatu against the coalition's leadership, helmed by PAS.
Bersatu also has one exco post each in Kedah and Terengganu.
Separately, Bersatu's Kijal assemblyman, Razali Idris, said he was ready to step down from the Terengganu exco if asked to do so by menteri besar Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar.
Samsuri, a PAS vice-president, was also the PN chairman before its deregistration.
Razali said he had stated this stance after PAS ended its political cooperation with Bersatu in June.

Razali, who holds the tourism, culture, environment and climate change portfolio, previously stepped down as Terengganu Bersatu chief and hinted at leaving the party after the state assembly dissolves.
4f53d719624d40c1: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is continuing to disburse financial assistance in stages under the Paddy Crop Takaful Scheme (STTP) to registered farmers affected by drought this year.
The Agriculture and Food Security Ministry (KPKM) said RM1.99 million had been paid in stages to farmers in areas under the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (MADA) from June until this month.
Another RM5.13 million in aid for farmers outside Mada areas will be distributed in stages from Oct 23.

"The welfare of padi farmers remains a priority for the government, including addressing the effects of drought and delays in fertiliser supplies in Mada areas," the ministry said in a statement today.
On the delays in fertiliser supplies in Mada areas, the ministry said any assessment of their impact on padi production must be based on actual yield data rather than assumptions.

It said a preliminary analysis of 21 per cent of samples from Mada's Crop Cutting Survey (CCS) estimated the average gross yield for Season 1/2026 at 5.69 tonnes per hectare, compared with 4.60 tonnes per hectare in Season 1/2025.
"These preliminary findings show an increase in average gross yield across Mada and, so far, do not indicate an overall decline in yields.
"However, the figures are still preliminary and cannot be regarded as a definitive conclusion on the impact of fertiliser supply delays on individual farmers," it said.
The ministry said a comprehensive study would be conducted after harvesting was completed in November to obtain a more complete and accurate picture of padi production for the season.
It said any conclusions and follow-up measures must be objective, evidence-based and take into account farmers' interests and the sustainability of national padi production.
The ministry added that it would continue monitoring developments on the ground and ensure farmers' welfare remained a priority while safeguarding rice supply stability and national food security.
77d06fe1ce7d20bb: PETALING JAYA: A 16-year-old teenager who allegedly attacked a teacher at Tunku Putra-HELP International School (TPH) in Kuching this morning live streamed the incident on social media, police said.
Sarawak acting police commissioner Saifullizan Ishak said the recording, lasting 12 minutes and six seconds, showed the attack from the teenager’s perspective, reported Sinar Harian.
He said the video had since been removed by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission.
Saifullizan said police were investigating the case under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt with a dangerous weapon and Section 6(1) of the Explosives Act 1957.
He said the student had been detained and later released on police bail.
In a statement, the school said the teacher was in stable condition following the incident. It said students in the affected classroom managed to evacuate the area and no one else was injured.
The school was closed early as a precaution on police advice, and parents were notified to collect their children.
“As of now, the teacher is recovering well and has sustained no critical injuries.
“TPH is deeply grateful for our teacher’s bravery and composure during the incident, and wishes her a full recovery.
“The student suspected of being involved in the incident is no longer an active TPH student,” it said.
The school confirmed that classes would resume tomorrow after receiving clearance from the authorities. It said it had reviewed its safety protocols and tightened security measures.
Three auxiliary police officers will be stationed on the school grounds, while appropriate security checks will be conducted on people entering the campus.
The school is also considering more comprehensive long-term security measures.
Its senior leadership team will hold assemblies to explain the incident, address students’ concerns, and arrange counselling support for those who need it.
Separately, the Sarawak education department said it had contacted the school and was prepared to provide support to those affected.
8838056fc4e01dcc: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are awaiting further instructions from the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) on their investigation into allegations that Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was coerced into signing an Instrument of Proclamation.
In a written reply published on the Parliament website, the Home Ministry said the investigation papers were referred to the A-GC on Sept 29 for review and further instructions.
It said further police action would depend on the outcome of the review and the A-GC's directives.

"Police will take appropriate action in accordance with the prevailing laws, and the Home Ministry assures that the investigation is being conducted professionally, transparently and in compliance with the law, without favouring any party," it said.
Cha Kee Chin (PH-Rasah) had asked for an update on the investigation into Ismail's Sept 8 police report and the action taken or to be taken against those involved.
The ministry said police had recorded statements from four individuals to assist in the investigation.
On Sept 9, Ismail alleged that he had been coerced into signing an Instrument of Proclamation intended to remove the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
The government aims to complete the registration of all refugees under the Domestic Refugee Registration Document Programme by Dec 31, 2029.
The Home Ministry said 4,010 individuals had been registered under the programme's first phase as of June, following its implementation on Jan 1 this year.
Of the total, 4,008 were from Myanmar, while one each was from Sudan and Syria.

The ministry said 400 individuals had been transferred to the Special Isolation Centre for Refugees and Asylum Seekers in Bidor, Perak, for the status determination process, while 78 had been granted refugee status.

It said the second phase of the Foreign National Registration Programme would cover individuals outside immigration detention depots, including holders of United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees cards and those claiming to be refugees.
"Based on the announced plans, this phase is scheduled to commence in the second half of this year, with the entire registration process targeted for completion by Dec 31, 2029.

"The implementation encompasses the collection of personal information and biometrics, security screening, as well as a process for the government to determine and verify individuals' status," the ministry said. -- BERNAMA
0ddda4543527f4f6: WASHINGTON: OpenAI has revealed that two of its AI agents disabled or weakened systems built to catch them misbehaving, with one later denying it had done so.
The cases are the latest in a string of safety scares at the world's top AI developers involving agents, AI programmes that carry out tasks without human involvement.

In a report released Tuesday, the ChatGPT maker said that during two internal coding jobs, its agents switched off or undermined tools for detecting incidents of AI models acting against human wishes.

On Oct 3, an agent running on OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol model, which had been told not to send any messages on the workplace chat app, took that as licence to switch off safety alerts meant for the company's security team while fixing a testing system.
Three days later, a GPT-6 Astra agent stripped out its own monitor while copying code from another project, then told the human programmer it had done no such thing.
The company said it had also seen several cases of agents launching software with monitoring switched off, exposing a gap in its oversight.
OpenAI said it is still trying to determine whether the models were simply overzealous in following instructions or have a particular tendency to evade monitoring.
"We don't yet have a satisfying explanation for this behaviour," it said.
The disclosure adds to mounting unease over how well leading labs can control increasingly autonomous systems.

In July, a group of OpenAI agents broke out of their test environments and launched a cyberattack on AI firm Hugging Face, causing international alarm. Other companies have since reported similar incidents.
The incidents have fuelled calls in the United States and abroad for tighter oversight of AI development.
But US President Donald Trump, under the advice of top AI executives like Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, has urged the industry to police itself.

890515901a45b61b: PETALING JAYA: Kertas siasatan berhubung dakwaan Menteri Besar Negeri Sembilan, Ismail Lasim, dipaksa menandatangani proklamasi bagi menyingkirkan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan kini di Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC).
Menteri Dalam Negeri, Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, berkata polis telah mengambil keterangan empat individu bagi membantu siasatan dan kertas siasatan itu dirujuk kepada AGC pada 29 Sept lalu.
"Polis sedang menunggu keputusan serta arahan lanjut AGC berkenaan kertas siasatan tersebut. Sebarang tindakan dan siasatan lanjut polis tertakluk kepada hasil penelitian dan arahan AGC.
"Polis akan mengambil tindakan sewajarnya selaras peruntukan undang-undang berkuatkuasa," katanya dalam jawapan bertulis di Parlimen.
Saifuddin menjawab pertanyaan Cha Kee Chin (PH-Rasah) berhubung status terkini siasatan ke atas laporan polis dibuat Ismail pada 8 Sept lalu.

Pada 5 Sept lalu, empat undang dipertikaikan itu mendakwa Ismail menandatangani proklamasi bagi menyingkirkan Tuanku Muhriz, walaupun Ismail mengelak daripada mengulas dakwaan berkenaan dan berikrar taat setia sepenuhnya kepada pemerintah negeri.
Tiga hari kemudian, undang terbabit menunjukkan dokumen didakwa proklamasi yang ditandatangani Ismail dalam satu sidang media.
Ismail kemudian mendakwa beliau menandatangani dokumen itu "tanpa rela hati dan secara paksaan", sambil menegaskan proklamasi terbabit tidak sah. Beliau turut membuat laporan polis.
Bagaimanapun, beliau kemudian menyokong kenyataan Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri yang mengumumkan penyingkiran Tuanku Muhriz sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan.
a25875e508ad8e84: Nearly two-thirds of US doctors are turning to an AI-powered search engine to make patient decisions, propelling a little-known tech startup to a $15 billion valuation while prompting a debate over the future of patient care.

Miami-based OpenEvidence, founded by serial entrepreneur Daniel Nadler in 2022, said that many of America’s 1 million physicians processed more than 42 million prompts last month. Doctors are using the company’s chatbot to scour medical journals and clinical guidelines to help diagnose and treat patients.

The ads-powered platform has grown largely by word of mouth, penetrating a sector where few tools have seen similar traction. “We’re the first viral consumer internet app in healthcare,” Nadler told the FT in an interview.
52842e009da6f020: PHP developers have released emergency updates for two critical vulnerabilities after cybersecurity authorities warned organizations to patch immediately or consider taking exposed applications offline.
PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 address CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. The project's developers urged users to update immediately.

All PHP installations serving web requests are potentially affected, including deployments using PHP-FPM, Apache's mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed, the developers said. "We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs."

Jake Knott, head of threat intelligence at watchTowr, said: "As expected, watchTowr Intel is already observing in-the-wild exploitation of the latest PHP vulnerabilities, with a variety of vibecoded PoCs already hitting our sensors featuring a variety of 'php2shell' User-Agents. Whilst nobody has been successful to date, we don't expect that will last long."

"Where immediate patching is not feasible, organizations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is available," CERT-EU said in an advisory issued ahead of the patches. The body lists both vulnerabilities with CVSS scores of 9.2.

Finnish government services and websites belonging to the Dutch parliament, cybersecurity authorities, and data protection regulator were taken offline as a precaution. Privacy campaign group noyb also temporarily withdrew its website.

PHP "powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," infosec vendor Huntress noted.

That makes identifying exposed installations a substantial job. "The number of places you have to go looking to identify vulnerable PHP versions gets very big, very fast," said John Hammond, Huntress's senior principal security researcher. ®
f4047fad45ddb75e: PETALING JAYA: A final-year college student was found dead in Lukut, Negeri Sembilan, today, believed to have fallen from a height.
Port Dickson police chief Ahmad Afiq Adnan said the 21-year-old student was undergoing practical training at a hotel in Lukut, and was found dead behind an eatery at 6.05am.
"An autopsy ruled that the cause of death was injuries to the head and abdomen resulting from a fall from a height. Checks found no criminal elements," Bernama quoted him as saying.
Afiq said the student was renting a room on the third floor of a building near where the body was found. Police found no signs of a break-in, and the victim's personal belongings were intact.
The case has been classified as sudden death.

0d1c59b202fa5211: GENEVA: The El Nino weather phenomenon gripping the planet is heading off the charts, the UN warned Wednesday, saying countries should take urgent action to prepare for the worst.
El Nino is set to peak in December, but the human impact of its associated extreme temperatures, floods and droughts is set to last into 2027 and beyond.
The UN called for international preventative measures to protect the millions of people most exposed – before disaster strikes.

"The current El Nino event could be unprecedented in strength: literally off the monitoring charts that we have used for the past four decades," said Celeste Saulo, head of the UN's weather and climate agency.

"We are already witnessing extreme weather events and expect this to multiply and cascade as El Nino intensifies," the World Meteorological Organization chief told a press conference in Geneva, alongside UN aid chief Tom Fletcher.
They issued a joint call for "urgent and coordinated anticipatory action" to protect the most vulnerable communities already living on the edge.
"We cannot stop El Nino, but we can prevent many of its worst human consequences," said Saulo.
'Wrecking ball'
Fletcher said El Nino was a "wrecking ball" that would bring havoc to Latin America, eastern and southern Africa, Asia and the Pacific.
He said the long-term impact "will be felt for months and potentially years to come... because it's this overlaying of crisis on crisis and crisis".
He cited widespread conflict and displacement, soaring fuel and fertiliser and food prices, and swingeing aid cuts.
"The risk is you have tens of millions of people pushed into humanitarian need," he explained, warning that 50 million people could face increased hunger.
Fletcher said the next two weeks were "the critical window to act".

Somalia, Ethiopia, and Kenya need supplies ahead of heavy rains; southern Africa needs seeds and livestock. Central America needs livelihood assistance, while Asia and the Pacific must prepare for droughts, floods and cyclones, he said.
However, Fletcher warned that the damage from El Nino would not be limited to countries on the front line.
"It will create economic shocks for the global economy and drive further conflict, displacement, migration," he said.
"I am sounding the alarm that the humanitarian system... cannot alone cope with a threat on this scale."
He called on countries, development banks and international financial institutions to get money moving "before that damage is done".
Fletcher said he had released US$50 million to help 11 countries on the frontline, including Chad, El Salvador, Ethiopia, Somalia and South Sudan.
'Far-reaching consequences'
El Nino warms surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, bringing worldwide changes in winds, pressure and rainfall patterns.
It typically takes place every two to seven years and lasts around nine to 12 months.
Conditions oscillate between El Nino and its opposite La Nina, with neutral conditions in between.
The naturally occurring weather phenomenon is set to bring higher temperatures to much of the planet, with its impact compounding the effects of man-made climate change.

The WMO's latest global seasonal climate update out Wednesday forecasted that sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific Ocean – the epicentre of El Nino – may rise to 3.8°C above average during November to January: way above typical El Nino figures.
This would be the highest three-month measurement since observations began, eclipsing the previous record of 2.6°C set in 2015-2016.
"This will have far-reaching consequences for weather patterns across the world," said Saulo.
While El Nino usually peaks between November and February, the resulting spike in temperatures typically comes later.
The last El Nino contributed to making 2023 the second-hottest year on record and 2024 the all-time high.
This El Nino is already hitting some regions hard, including in Central America, where animals and crops are dying from drought.

f8c1607d9284d7f3: PETALING JAYA: A total of 13,072 doctor positions in the health ministry remained vacant as of June 30, comprising 1,660 specialist posts and 11,412 non-specialist positions, said health minister Dzulkefly Ahmad.
Dzulkefly said 3,510 medical officers resigned between 2024 and 2026, comprising 1,252 permanent and 2,258 contract doctors.
Of those who resigned, 51.4% left for the private sector, while 36.8% cited personal reasons, and 4.5% joined statutory bodies.
Another 2.9% left to work or settle overseas, 2.6% resigned for health reasons, 1.5% pursued further studies, and 0.3% opened their own clinics.
He also said eight medical specialists had resigned or migrated overseas.

Dzulkefly said this in a written parliamentary reply to a question from V Ganabatirau (PH-Klang) on doctors resigning or migrating overseas, vacancies, specialist shortages, waiting times for housemanship placements, and the effectiveness of measures to retain doctors.
He said the ministry had appointed 14,064 permanent and 9,847 contract medical officers during the same period.
To address staffing shortages, he said, 4,500 contract doctors had been offered permanent appointments this year.

Dzulkefly said a task force established by the public services department in April was looking into staffing issues, while the ministry had been given greater authority to manage and distribute approved positions to speed up recruitment.
Dzulkefly said six government hospitals had met a target of treating at least 70% of non-emergency patients within two hours, compared with the average waiting time of four to six hours previously.
In a written reply to Dr Zulkafperi Hanapi (Ind-Tanjong Karang), he said Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital in Ipoh recorded the highest rate with 98.61% of green zone patients treated within two hours.

This was followed by Ampang Hospital (88.78%), Selayang Hospital (74.1%), Sultanah Aminah Hospital in Johor Bahru (73.2%), Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital in Klang (72.2%) and Kuala Lumpur Hospital (71.8%).
He also highlighted a 9% reduction in patient attendance at six major hospitals following the extension of operating hours at selected government health clinics.
The clinics operate until 9pm on weekdays and from 8am to 1pm on weekends and public holidays.
The extended hours had helped divert patients with minor ailments from hospital emergency departments, he said.
Dzulkefly also said all eight initiatives under the special task force on agency reform to reduce hospital overcrowding had been fully implemented as of June.

Other measures include outsourcing treatment to private general practitioners, expanding digital screening for non-emergency patients before they visit clinics to 545 health clinics, and improving patient flow at government hospitals.
65c4c44041192d4a: Cute robots stole the show at Nvidia's GTC keynote in Berlin, where Jensen Huang pitched a future powered by AI agents – and, naturally, plenty of his company's hardware.
The Nvidia chief remained his usual ebullient self despite environmental protesters interrupting his presentation at Berlin's tent-shaped Tempodrom.
"Why don't you clean up your act?" they demanded, holding up banners that partially obscured the presentation screen behind Huang.
"All important issues, but let me get through my keynote," he joked, adding: "I'll talk to you guys later," as security swiftly removed them.
Huang was discussing Vera Rubin systems before unveiling DSX POD, a reference design for factory-built, containerized AI infrastructure.

DSX POD combines seven liquid-cooled Vera Rubin compute racks using Nvidia's Spectrum-X networking. Partners will cable, integrate, and test the systems in modular containers before delivery, with availability expected in early 2027.

Nvidia claims deployment could shrink from six months to as little as 14 days at a prepared site. That excludes the not insignificant matter of getting power, connectivity, and other site infrastructure ready first.

He was keen to add that Vera Rubin systems are designed for closed-loop liquid cooling with coolant temperatures up to 45°C, while outdoor dry coolers release heat into the air without needing to evaporate water. "At 2 gigawatts, DSX can save 54 million litres of water a day," Huang claimed, perhaps thinking of those environmental protesters.
Yet much of the leather-jacketed leader's attention was focused on physical AI: robots, autonomous vehicles, and other machinery Nvidia hopes to supply with its hardware and software.

The Microducks from Pollen Robotics are small, two-legged robots with cameras for faces. Huang interacted with them on stage, getting them to lie down and roll over by voice command, and the little robots all beeped back at him in response.
The robo ducks demonstrated a workflow in which AI was trained in the cloud, evaluated on an Nvidia RTX Spark PC, then deployed on the robots.

Huang also unveiled Agile ONE SN, a humanoid robot reference platform from German robotics startup Agile Robots, based on Nvidia's Isaac GR00T technology and a Jetson Thor compute module. Scheduled for early 2027, the platform is intended to give robotics researchers and developers a ready-made system for developing and testing capabilities.
"This is going to be the next major industry, the next great industry," Huang claimed.

Beyond robots, Nvidia is pushing its AI hardware and software into cars and telecoms networks. Huang boasted that Nvidia's Hyperion car system is being adopted by more vendors, saying: "We turned this into an industry standard, and now it's being designed into one car fleet after another."

Europe's telecoms operators are also deploying Nvidia-powered computing in their networks to deliver advanced services using AI-RAN, according to Huang. "After working on this for nearly eight years, Nvidia made the first commercial phone call on the T-Mobile network with Nokia, and so now CUDA makes phone calls," he said.
Far from slowing down the progression of AI, it seems Nvidia is determined to push its technology into every corner of the world. "Everyone will become an AI company," Huang claimed.

He also took care to praise Europe and its technology efforts while he was in Berlin. "As expected, Jensen positioned Nvidia as a strong supporter of – and enabler for – Europe's sovereign tech ambitions. Nvidia has invested almost $10 billion into Europe in the past year, including 14 investments into European startups during Jensen's current trip," said Forrester principal analyst Paul Miller.

But Miller pointed out that Nvidia itself is not European. "Anything with critical ongoing dependencies on Nvidia (or any other non-European firm) is unlikely to meet the purest definitions of European tech sovereignty," he added.
Huang closed with a CGI video of robots performing a Eurovision-style song recapping his keynote. Yes, it was as bad as you imagine. ®

5d50bdb9f42e99c2: PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) lacks the manpower needed to optimally manage the country's borders, home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today.
Saifuddin said the agency was still strengthening its organisation after taking over the border control role from various agencies, including the immigration department and the customs department.
"As of Sept 23, AKPS had 8,403 personnel, a number seen as insufficient for optimal operations in managing all of the country's 123 entry points," he said in a written parliamentary reply.
He said the home ministry was creating and filling new posts, prioritising operations at entry points with higher risks, traffic, and cargo.
These posts would be filled in phases over the next five years.
The agency was also rationalising and optimising personnel deployment based on risk factors and actual operational needs to ensure efficient use of human resources without affecting border security.
"AKPS is also continuing to work with other core agencies in this transition period, including for operational coordination, resource sharing and enforcement support as needed," he said.
He was replying to Khlir Nor (Bersatu-Ketereh), who asked about the ministry's measures to address AKPS's manpower shortage.
AKPS was allocated 8,403 positions at its launch.

22142f8e91cd1525: Microsoft is raising OneDrive's supported macOS sync limit to one million items, matching Windows, alongside new Copilot features, sharing controls, and an admin command-line tool.

The macOS preview is scheduled for the Insiders ring this month, with general availability targeted for June 2027. Eligible devices must meet hardware and configuration requirements; others retain the existing 300,000-item supported limit.
"This increase is intended to help organizations with large OneDrive and SharePoint libraries sync more content reliably across devices," Microsoft said.

However, sync performance may suffer for large numbers of read-only files or accounts under legal hold. "We are actively working to improve performance and reliability for these scenarios," Microsoft said.
Microsoft's cull of OneDrive's File Explorer shortcuts wasn't a retreat from AI. Its latest announcement gives Copilot more to do.

The assistant can now be asked to analyze across files (for example, selecting several spreadsheets and getting the bot to come up with charts and graphs), told to organize folders, or save a repeated workflow as a personal skill in a Markdown file. There is also a Prompt Gallery to save the user from having to come up with their own ideas.

Perhaps most interesting is the addition of "Hero Links," designed to end the proliferation of links to files and folders in OneDrive as permission needs change. The feature provides one link per file and folder by default, with permissions that can be updated while keeping the same URL.
Automatic expiration controls are still coming, however. Organizations that require time-limited access will want to check that gap before adopting the feature.

Administrators also get a OneDrive Sync command-line tool, available in private preview, for inspecting accounts, configuration, policies, and sync status. The tool can pull information from the OneDrive sync client and provide data on status, policy troubleshooting, and issue diagnosis, from folder backup and policy problems on a single PC to identifying devices that need attention across an organization.
And yes, there is, of course, integration with AI agents. ®
fb9b192333f438c2: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Authorities should examine how much ship emissions contribute to air pollution around major ports, particularly during haze episodes originating from Indonesia, says maritime industry expert Datuk Seri Jeyenderan M. Ramasamy.

Jeyenderan, the chief executive officer of Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, said Malaysia’s strategic location along the Strait of Malacca, one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes, offered significant opportunities to develop its marine fuel supply sector, but environmental considerations should not be overlooked.

“As more vessels pass through our waters, we should ensure that ship emissions are properly monitored and that our ports develop sustainably. The environmental impact of shipping activity deserves closer attention, particularly when transboundary haze affects Malaysia,” he said in a statement.
He said Port Klang and ports in Johor were strategically positioned along international shipping routes, giving Malaysia the opportunity to attract more vessels to bunker locally.

However, ships burning heavy fuel oil, including high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO), can release air pollutants such as sulphur oxides, particulate matter and other combustion-related pollutants, depending on the fuel used and engine operating conditions.
The International Maritime Organization (IMO) introduced a global sulphur limit of 0.50 per cent by mass for fuel used by ships outside designated emission control areas from January 1, 2020.

Ships may use higher-sulphur fuel if they operate under the applicable rules with an approved exhaust gas cleaning system, commonly called a scrubber. The limit for fuel used on board is separate from the rules governing HSFO carried as cargo.

Jeyenderan said the relevant authorities could consider monitoring air quality around major ports, checking compliance with marine fuel sulphur limits and studying pollution levels during haze episodes to better understand the contribution of different sources.

He stressed that reliable monitoring data would help policymakers distinguish between pollution from transboundary haze and emissions from local sources, including shipping, while supporting efforts to balance the maritime industry’s growth with environmental protection.

Echoing the call, Universiti Malaysia Terengganu adjunct professor Nazery Khalid urged the authorities to closely monitor ship emissions during haze episodes, saying Malaysia’s efforts to attract more vessels and expand seaborne trade should not come at the expense of meeting its emissions targets and its international commitments to combat climate change.

“As a responsible maritime nation and a long-standing member of the International Maritime Organization Council, Malaysia is duty-bound to ensure maritime operations in its waters are carried out in an eco-friendly manner, in full adherence to national laws and international standards.

“By ensuring emissions from shipping activities are closely monitored, even during the haze, Malaysia can also underscore its commitment to meeting its net-zero target by 2050. Shipping, which facilitates close to 90 per cent of its trade, and the maritime industry in general can play a leading role in realising this national agenda by operating sustainably,” said Nazery in the joint statement.
He also urged maritime industry stakeholders to take great care to protect the health and well-being of workers, while ensuring activities are not too severely disrupted amid the worsening haze.

“Workers involved in outdoor activities such as shipping, port operations at berthing areas and dockyards, shipbuilding or ship repair, and offshore operations should ensure their health is not compromised while carrying out their tasks,” he said.
ff022620b2ebf6ca: ALLAGASH (US), Oct 21 — Early snow is already dusting the north-easternmost US state of Maine, where a canny 73-year-old Republican senator is having to run the race of her life to help save Donald Trump’s party from being frozen out of power nationwide.
Susan Collins has held her Senate seat for three decades, becoming a near immovable fixture in the state’s political landscape.

But with President Trump deeply unpopular nationwide and Mainers furious about surging fuel prices ahead of winter, Collins’s Democratic challenger is eying an upset — and a chance to make his party’s outside bid to regain the Senate a reality.
The stakes are enormous in the race between Collins and logger-turned-politician Troy Jackson, as Maine is crucial for any Democratic path to a US Senate majority.

While Democrats are forecast to win the House of Representatives in the November 3 midterms, they would need to clinch the Senate too if they want to stop Trump’s right-wing agenda in its tracks, including his power to nominate Supreme Court justices.
Time for change?
About one-third of Maine’s voters are unaffiliated with either party. Because independents generally are opposed to Trump nationwide, that could work to Jackson’s advantage.
Most voters interviewed by AFP agreed that Collins had done well in funneling federal funding back to Maine over the years and that 58-year-old newcomer Jackson would not be so successful.

But like many Mainers, retired teacher Louisa Beckett believes a perfect storm of national setbacks — cost-of-living hikes, the Iran war, and allegations of massive Trump corruption — could finally sink Collins.
“She does a lot for the state of Maine,” Beckett said while attending a “No Kings” anti-Trump rally.
“However this is much, much bigger than the state of Maine,” added the 80-year-old. “It’s about our democracy, it’s about our Constitution.”
Divided communities
Both Collins and Jackson hail from the same sparsely populated, heavily forested northern county of Aroostook, bordering Canada.
Logging, hunting and cross-border trade are the focuses there — but these days, so is politics and the price of fuel.
Fiery arguments have broken out among patrons at Rock’s Family Diner in the Aroostook frontier town of Fort Kent.
The divisions are even visible in Jackson’s remote hometown of Allagash, where red Collins signs are visible outside some houses in the community of 227 people.
Hilton Hafford, 68, said he was all for his local friend Jackson, but added with a grimace: “My sisters and brother are on the other side.”
A retired logger who guides moose hunts, Hafford said Jackson will be the best to push back against Trump in Washington.
But Collins’s main pitch is that despite being a Republican she has already proven sufficiently independent from Trump’s most extreme policies.

“The most remarkable thing she manages to do is to insulate herself from the unpopularity of a president in the same political party,” University of Southern Maine political science professor Ron Schmidt told AFP.
“Even the (Mainers) who aren’t crazy about her have a certain amount of ‘the devil you know is better than the devil you don’t’ attitude towards her.”
And yet some experts believe Collins is deeply vulnerable, with diesel and heating oil prices soaring.
Maine is America’s most heating oil-dependent state, and residents expressed outrage at how fixed-income households could suffer this winter.
‘Hardcore Democrat’ for Collins
Maine has not backed a Republican presidential candidate since 1988, but it’s far from a Democratic stronghold, with voters regularly choosing Republicans for Congress.
In Collins’s hometown of Caribou, brewery owner and Collins supporter Shawn Pelletier said the senator does face “a lot of headwind.”
But Collins retains considerable loyalty from across society.
“My father is a hardcore Democrat, and he has a Susan Collins sign on his lawn,” Pelletier said.

Part of the appeal, said Brandon Lane, a 37-year-old who runs outdoor adventures company Allagash Guide Service, is that Collins exerts her power in Washington to help Maine, including negotiating exemptions on Canadian goods like road salt.
“With Susan Collins, you know what you’re getting,” he told AFP.
Polls show the candidates mostly neck and neck. Yet Maine is notoriously hard to poll accurately — and Collins is a survivor.
In 2020 she trailed her Democratic challenger in pre-election polling. Then she won by nine points. — AFP
00c0289996c374cc: ISTANBUL, Oct 21 — US researchers have developed an artificial intelligence tool that can predict cancer patients’ survival chances from a single facial photograph, according to a study published Monday in the journal The Lancet Digital Health, Anadolu Ajansi reported.

Developed by researchers at Mass General Brigham in the US state of Massachusetts, the system, called FAHR-Face, analyses facial features to estimate biological age and mortality risk, potentially helping doctors make treatment decisions.

The model was trained on more than 40 million facial photos and adapted into two tools: FAHR-FaceAge, which estimates biological age, and FAHR-FaceSurvival, which predicts cancer patients’ survival directly from facial images without relying on age estimates.

Researchers found that the survival model focused mainly on areas beneath the eyes and around the nose, while the age-estimation model examined facial features around the mouth and temples, suggesting the two systems identify different health-related patterns.
The survival model was trained on images of 34,363 patients and tested on another 3,820, with results independently validated using data from 4,892 cancer patients in the Netherlands.
Researchers found that patients classified in the highest-risk group had more than three times the mortality risk of those in the lowest-risk group, even after accounting for clinical factors.

Patients whose faces appeared at least five years older than their actual age also had a 21 per cent higher mortality risk, while those appearing at least five years younger had a 17 per cent lower risk.
Combining the two models further improved the accuracy of survival predictions, according to the study.

Researchers said the technology could help doctors assess patients’ health and guide treatment decisions, although further validation is needed before it can be widely used in clinical practice. — Bernama-Anadolu
2ae0d3b75b3c2ee5: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Matcha, a powdered Japanese green tea that once dominated the beverage scene, particularly at trendy cafes before making its way to roadside stalls, is now gaining wider popularity in the culinary industry.
No longer confined to lattes, fancy drinks and desserts, matcha is increasingly being incorporated into a variety of savoury dishes, including nasi lemak, burgers and even fried catfish.
While such combinations may sound unusual, they have found their own following, with some consumers embracing the notion that “the greener, the healthier”.

But does this growing trend of matcha-infused dishes represent creative culinary innovation and a healthier way of eating, or is it simply a marketing strategy to attract attention and gain popularity on social media?
Innovation or healthy eating?

Senior lecturer at the Department of Science and Mathematics, Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia, Dr Adnin Afifi Nawi, views the current phenomenon primarily as a form of culinary creativity aimed at attracting customers.
He said that although matcha has antioxidant properties, various factors must be considered before labelling matcha-containing dishes as “healthy diet” options.

“If a food item goes viral because of its attractive colour or unique taste, there is nothing wrong with giving it a try. However, we should not immediately conclude that it is healthy simply because it contains matcha,” he told Bernama.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

No longer confined to lattes, fancy drinks and desserts, matcha is increasingly being incorporated into a variety of savoury dishes, including ‘nasi lemak’, burgers and even fried catfish. — Social media pic

Observing that consumer preferences have evolved, he said the elements of being “unique” and “visually appealing”, particularly when shared on social media, have become priorities among young people today.

“In the past, we chose food based on taste and quality, but purchasing behaviour has changed. Today, being ‘unique’ and ‘beautiful’ enough to post on TikTok or Instagram has become a priority. In the digital economy, consumer attention is a goldmine.
“The more unusual or extraordinary a dish is, the greater its potential to be shared and go viral.

“Matcha’s vibrant green colour makes it highly photogenic. If a food picture or video manages to captivate netizens within the first three seconds, the dish is likely to become highly sought after,” he said.
He added that international media had reported the growing global popularity of matcha, with demand for the ingredient outstripping supply.
“Reports by the South China Morning Post have also revealed that some traditional producers in Japan are struggling to meet surging global demand, fuelled by the influence of social media,” he said.
Understanding matcha

Explaining the health benefits of matcha from a scientific perspective, Professor Dr Norsham Juliana Nordin, an expert in chronophysiology and chrononutrition at the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences, Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia, said matcha is a powdered green tea derived from the Camellia sinensis plant and contains catechins, which are potent antioxidants.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Matcha’s vibrant green colour makes it highly photogenic. — AFP pic

Consuming foods containing catechins may help reduce inflammation in the body, boost metabolism, support weight management, and promote heart and blood vessel health. Matcha also has natural antibacterial and antiviral properties.
However, the nutrition expert stressed that the health value of a dish cannot be determined solely by the presence of a single ingredient considered beneficial.
Instead, she said, a balanced approach to healthy eating requires consideration of the overall composition of a meal, including portion size, preparation methods, frequency of consumption and timing.

“Matcha does have a sound nutritional basis because it contains polyphenols, particularly catechins such as epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), as well as L-theanine and caffeine. Its use is therefore not merely a gimmick.
“However, when matcha is added to nasi lemak, burgers, noodles, traditional cakes or desserts, we cannot automatically assume that the entire dish has become a ‘health food’.

“The nutritional value is still determined by the overall dish. If only a small amount of matcha is added while the food remains high in calories, sugar, saturated fat or sodium, the overall nutritional impact does not change dramatically,” she told Bernama.
Matcha ‘nasi lemak’ and fried catfish

On viral food creations such as matcha nasi lemak and matcha-marinated fried catfish, Norsham Juliana said matcha has strong sensory appeal, with its green colour, umami flavour and slight bitterness lending dishes a premium image.
However, adding the ingredient to nasi lemak or fried catfish does not necessarily make either dish healthier.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

File picture showing bags of tea in a tea processing factory in Sayama, Japan. Excessive matcha consumption could cause caffeine-sensitive individuals to experience headaches, palpitations, restlessness and difficulty sleeping. — AFP pic

“For nasi lemak, the calorie, fat and sodium content, as well as portion size, still depend on the amount of coconut milk, sambal, anchovies and oil used, and how much is consumed. Adding matcha to the rice may contribute some polyphenols and introduce a variation in flavour and colour, but it does not ‘neutralise’ the coconut milk, salt or excess calories.

“A more meaningful way to make nasi lemak more balanced is to control portion size and the amount of coconut milk, oil and sodium used, while adding vegetables or cucumber. Choosing healthier cooking methods for the accompanying dishes would also help. Matcha can then be included as a creative addition.
“In other words, matcha may add value, but it is not a licence to disregard the nutritional composition of the entire meal,” she said.
The same applies to catfish prepared using matcha as a marinade.

She said matcha could contribute phenolic compounds, flavour and colour to the fish, but clinical evidence remains insufficient to claim that matcha-marinated catfish offers greater health benefits than conventionally prepared catfish.

“The greater difference to health usually comes from how the fish is cooked. Catfish marinated in matcha but deep-fried in large amounts of oil is still affected by the quantity of oil used, frying temperature, portion size and accompanying sauces.
“By contrast, grilled, baked or roasted fish prepared with controlled amounts of oil and salt generally has a better nutritional profile,” she explained.
At the same time, Norsham Juliana cautioned that exposing matcha to excessively high temperatures could reduce some of its beneficial properties.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

According to Professor Dr Norsham Juliana Nordin, an expert in chronophysiology and chrononutrition at the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences, Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia, high doses or the use of highly concentrated green tea extracts should not be regarded in the same way as ordinary food consumption. — AFP pic

“Catechins are not immune to heat. A study on matcha-enriched biscuits found that baking reduced the total catechin content by about 19 per cent compared with the dough. A bread study, meanwhile, showed that a substantial proportion of certain catechins could be retained after baking, although EGCG and epigallocatechin (EGC) were more susceptible to degradation than some other catechins,” she said.

“More precisely, cooking can reduce or alter some of matcha’s bioactive compounds, but it does not necessarily eliminate all of them. The higher the temperature and the longer the exposure, the greater the likelihood of changes occurring,” she added.
The risks of too much matcha
While enjoying matcha-infused dishes, consumers should also be aware of the potential risks associated with excessive consumption of foods containing the ingredient.

“Many people assume that ‘this cake contains matcha, so it must be healthier’, or that ‘this drink is green, so I can drink it frequently’. Another common mistake is overlooking the quantity consumed.

“In reality, the benefits and risks depend on the dose. A small serving is not the same as drinking several strong matcha beverages a day in addition to eating matcha desserts,” Norsham Juliana explained.
Citing the European Food Safety Authority, she said the consumption of 800 milligrammes or more of EGCG daily through food supplements had been associated with increased liver enzyme levels.

“High doses or the use of highly concentrated green tea extracts should not be regarded in the same way as ordinary food consumption. Safety assessments indicate that liver injury is rare, but particular attention is given to supplements or concentrated extracts containing high doses of EGCG, especially when taken as a large single dose,” she stressed.
She also advised consumers to consider matcha’s caffeine content and the timing of consumption, particularly those who are sensitive to caffeine.

“A third common mistake is overlooking timing. From the perspective of chrononutrition and chronophysiology, both what we consume and when we consume it matter. Drinking matcha in the morning has different implications for sleep compared with consuming a caffeinated matcha beverage late at night,” she said.
She added that excessive matcha consumption could cause caffeine-sensitive individuals to experience headaches, palpitations, restlessness and difficulty sleeping.
“There is nothing wrong with enjoying matcha, but do not eat with your eyes alone. Its green colour is appealing, but health cannot be judged by colour or a single ingredient.
“If you choose a matcha drink, reduce the amount of sugar and syrup. If you opt for matcha cake or pastries, remember that they are still desserts and keep your portions under control,” she advised.
She recommended that consumers practise moderation rather than blindly subscribing to the notion that “the greener, the healthier”. — Bernama

ab754bf975bbc756: GENEVA, Oct 21 — Non-communicable diseases account for three-quarters of deaths worldwide but affect different population groups in different ways, a World Health Organization study showed on Tuesday.

In its biggest-ever look at inequality in health and non-communicable diseases (NCDs), the WHO studied the top four killers — cancer, cardiovascular diseases, chronic respiratory diseases and diabetes.
It also looked at the five main risk factors driving them — tobacco use, alcohol consumption, obesity, unhealthy diets, physical inactivity and air pollution.

The report then scanned this across differences in NCD burden, prevention and care — by age, gender, economic status, education, place of residence, disability status, employment and migration status.
“This is the first effort to systematically measure inequalities in NCDs and their risk factors on a global scale,” said Ahmad Reza Hosseinpoor, who leads the WHO’s health inequality monitoring team.
“The findings show which populations are being left behind.”
NCDs cover eight of the top 10 causes of death, with cardiovascular diseases the biggest killer by far, claiming almost 20 million deaths a year.

The 10 years of national data, collected between 2013 and 2022, confirmed that socio-economic status influences health at every stage — from initial exposure to risk factors, through to diagnosis, treatment and disease management.
For example, the report found that in low- and middle-income countries, less educated populations suffered higher rates of hypertension and diabetes.
Cervical cancer screening rates are very low among the poorest and least-educated women; while tobacco use remains higher among less-educated men than among more educated men.
Looking at geographical factors, the study found that people in rural areas has significantly more limited access to hypertension diagnosis and cancer screening.
Gender and age also play a role. Men with hypertension are diagnosed and treated less frequently than women, even though they consume more tobacco and alcohol.
Conversely, obesity is more common among women, particularly in developing countries.
The study confirmed that social marginalisation, disability and migrant status were significant factors contributing to increased risk.
The United Nations’ health agency urged governments to raise health-related taxes on tobacco, alcohol and sugary drinks — measures that are particularly effective among low-income populations.
Countries were also encouraged to tailor insurance schemes or subsidies for under-served communities and to incorporate inequality indicators into their national health systems. — AFP
97d1409c4dcd2f73: Generative AI is saving open source developers time while giving maintainers more rubbish to sift through, according to a Linux Foundation survey.
Respondents estimated that a quarter of incoming pull requests – proposed code changes – were low-quality "AI slop."

Open source projects have spent the past year grappling with AI-generated contributions, useful vulnerability discoveries, false positives, and duplicate reports. Linus Torvalds has warmed to the tools, while remaining critical of low-quality submissions.
The foundation argues that projects need clearer policies and better tools to handle the influx.

Almost three-quarters (71 percent) of maintainers reckon GenAI has lowered the barriers to contributing to open source, but just over half (53 percent) disagree that the technology has improved community trust. Respondents estimated that AI cut code-authoring time by 52 percent on average. But for highly complex tasks, 21 percent reported taking longer.

Then there is governance. Only 35 percent of projects have a formal policy permitting GenAI use, while 32 percent have no policy and no plans for one, leaving expectations unclear across much of the community.

Hilary Carter, SVP of Research at the Linux Foundation, said: "Open source projects need to design for a growing AI-generated contributor base, not simply react to it. That means setting clear expectations for GenAI, putting responsibility for testing and disclosure on contributors and giving maintainers better tools to manage incoming pull requests."
Among large projects, the estimated share of incoming pull requests classified as AI slop rises to 31 percent.

The workload extends beyond proposed code changes. The curl project announced this week it will move low and medium severity severity flaws to public view to protect a security team almost overwhelmed by AI-assisted reports.
Project maintainer Daniel Stenberg said: "We are struggling as a project as all key maintainers feel strained, overloaded and brought to the brink of what we can muster."
On the need for better tools for maintainers, Carter said: "If we get those fundamentals right, AI can expand participation without overburdening and increasing costs for maintainers." ®

5173075304e6b98c: TOKYO, Oct 21 — Global exports of the rare earth yttrium have stalled, causing what a Japanese official described as a “supply-demand crunch”, with the Financial Times reporting that Tokyo was months away from running out of the critical metal.
Yttrium is essential for manufacturing consumer electronics, LEDs, aviation engines, semiconductor production equipment and a variety of industrial products.
China accounts for almost two-thirds of rare earth mining production and 92 per cent of global refined output, according to the International Energy Agency.

“It is true that exports of yttrium have stalled not only to Japan but worldwide, causing a supply-demand crunch and soaring prices,” a Japanese industry ministry official told AFP today, on condition of anonymity.
“Exports to Japan have decreased, including delays in shipments, and the global volume itself is low,” the official said.
The comments came after the Financial Times reported that Japan could exhaust its supply of the critical material in “months”.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said in July that yttrium was “globally scarce” and was “an important rare earth for our country”.
According to Chinese customs data, exports of yttrium oxide to Japan amounted to 4,000 kilograms in September, compared with 51,000 kilograms in the same period the previous year.
The industry ministry official said Tokyo was working with the United States and European nations on critical mineral resources and rare earths, including yttrium.
Beijing has intensified pressure on Tokyo since Takaichi hinted last November that Japan could intervene militarily in any attack on self-ruled Taiwan.
China views Taiwan as its territory and has not ruled out taking it by force.

“China imposed export controls on Japan in accordance with laws and regulations, with the aim of curbing Japan’s attempts at remilitarisation and possessing nuclear weapons,” Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told a regular briefing today.

Japan has asked the US government and American businesses to press China to ease rare earth export controls to avoid “severe disruption to the global automotive, defence and chip industries”, the Financial Times report said.
US defence supply chains rely on Japanese components that use yttrium, the newspaper said. — AFP
05c8eb78562a8d38: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.
Introducing: the Impossible issue

We wanted our last print edition of 2026 to include a slate of stories that check in on impossible ideas. Why? Because it’s fun to dream about living on other planets or uploading our brains. But also because scientists and engineers who won’t give up on daring endeavors remind us what technology is supposed to do: make life better, safer, healthier, even more joyful.

That’s the ambition behind the stories in our new Impossible issue. We explore bold attempts to make synthetic blood, build cities on the moon, and attain cognitive immortality. We investigate AI’s ability to say no, a bionic eye that can restore sight, and high hopes for blended meat. Plus, we check in on six technologies that have been “coming soon” for years.

Astrolab’s upcoming rover will run the first LLMs on the moon

Large language models are set to go lunar. A computer capable of running AI software is one of the payloads aboard Astrolab’s FLIP lunar rover, which is slated to head to the moon as early as next month.

How to study a swiftly melting climate disaster

In Alaska’s Denali National Park, a 2013 lightning fire burned nearly 35,000 acres, stripping away the insulating layer that preserves permafrost. It’s given scientists a rare opportunity to study how fires reshape permafrost and carbon storage over time.

The work is providing critical clues into the complex mechanisms driving cascading climate feedback effects. As warming temperatures fuel fires, more permafrost thaws, releasing greenhouse-gas emissions that threaten to fuel more warming, fires and permafrost loss. Their observations are revealing worrisome signs about what lies ahead.
Discover what their fieldwork is revealing about a cascading climate disaster.
—James Temple
MIT Technology Review Narrated: the explosive claim that’s upended the AI world

“I think I have good news about the nature of neural networks.” With those simple words of optimism, Nick Cammarata, a researcher at AI startup Goodfire, kicked off a 26,000-word blog post that has knocked the industry on its head.
Cammarata claims that LLMs might be far easier to understand, and thus to monitor and control, than people previously thought. If true, it’s a huge deal. But not everyone is convinced.
